units.zh: 趙在禮，字翰臣，涿州人也。
units.en: Zhao Zaili, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Zhuozhou.
units.literal: Zhao Zaili, style name Hanchen, was a man of Zhuozhou.

units.zh: 曾祖景裕，祖士廉，皆不仕。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both held no office.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both did not take office.

units.zh: 父元德，盧臺軍使。
units.en: His father Yuande served as military commissioner of the Lu Terrace.
units.literal: His father Yuande was Lu Terrace military commissioner.

units.zh: 在禮始事燕帥劉仁恭為小校，唐光化末，仁恭遣其子守文逐浮陽節度使盧彥威，據其城，升在禮為軍使，以佐守文。
units.en: Zaili first entered service under the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer. At the end of the Tang Guanghua era, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to expel Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and occupy his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.
units.literal: Zaili at first served the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer; at the end of the Guanghua era of Tang, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to drive out Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and seize his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.

units.zh: 及守文死，事其子。
units.en: After Shouwen died, he served his son in turn.
units.literal: When Shouwen died, he served his son.

units.zh: 延祚為守光所害，守光子繼威復為部將張萬進所殺，在禮遂事萬進。
units.en: Yanzuo was killed by Liu Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was in turn killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then entered Wanjin's service.
units.literal: Yanzuo was killed by Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was again killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then served Wanjin.

units.zh: 萬進奔梁，在禮乃與滄州留後毛璋歸太原。
units.en: When Wanjin fled to Liang, Zaili returned to Taiyuan together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang.
units.literal: Wanjin fled to Liang; Zaili then together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang returned to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 同光末，為效節指揮使，屯於貝州。
units.en: At the end of the Tongguang era he was commander of the Xiaojie army, stationed at Beizhou.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang, he was Xiaojie army commander and was stationed at Beizhou.

units.zh: 會軍士皇甫暉等作亂，推指揮使楊晸為帥，晸不從，為眾所害，攜晸首以脅在禮。
units.en: When the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, they tried to make the commander Yang Zheng their leader. Zheng refused and was killed by the mutineers, who then brought his head to force Zaili to lead them.
units.literal: It happened that the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, pushing the commander Yang Zheng as leader; Zheng did not comply and was killed by the crowd, who carried Zheng's head to coerce Zaili.

units.zh: 在禮知其不可拒，遂從之，以四年二月六日引眾入鄴，在禮自稱留後。
units.en: Zaili knew he could not refuse, so he went along. On the sixth day of the second month of the fourth year he led his troops into Ye and styled himself acting prefect.
units.literal: Zaili knew it could not be refused, so he followed; on the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year he led the crowd into Ye, and Zaili styled himself acting prefect.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·張錫傳》：趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知棣州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。）〉
units.en: (The History of Song, biography of Zhang Xi, records that when Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, most of the prefectures along the river fell into disorder. Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou; he immediately paid out provincial funds to reward the troops, to general delight, and that prefecture alone remained secure—the people of Di were indebted to him.)〉
units.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Zhang Xi: When Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, the prefectures along the river for the most part stirred up disorder; Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou, immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the army, all were greatly pleased, and that one prefecture alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.)〉

units.zh: 唐莊宗遣明宗率師討之，會城下軍亂，在禮迎明宗入城，事具《唐書》。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang sent Emperor Mingzong at the head of an army against him. When the troops below the walls mutinied, Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city; the full account is in the Book of Tang.
units.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong sent Mingzong at the head of an army to attack him; it happened that the army below the walls mutinied, and Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city—the matter is fully set forth in the Book of Tang.

units.zh: 天成元年五月，授滑州節度使、檢校太保。
units.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng, he was appointed Huazhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 制下，在禮密奏軍情，未欲除移，且乞更伺少頃，尋就改天雄軍兵馬留後、鄴都留守、興唐尹。
units.en: When the appointment was announced, Zaili secretly reported on conditions in the army, saying he was not yet ready to be transferred and asking to wait a little longer. Soon afterward he was instead made acting commissioner of the Tianxiong army's horse and foot, garrison commander of the Ye capital, and prefect of Xingtang.
units.literal: When the edict was issued, Zaili secretly memorialized on military conditions, not yet wishing to be transferred, and moreover begged to wait a little longer; soon after he was changed to Tianxiong army acting commissioner of horse and foot, Ye capital garrison commander, and Xingtang prefect.

units.zh: 既而在禮將皇甫暉、趙進等相次除郡赴任，
units.en: Zaili then had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others appointed in succession to prefectural posts and sent off to take office,
units.literal: Afterward Zaili had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others in succession appointed to prefectures and sent to take up their posts,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·皇甫暉傳》：明宗即位，暉自軍卒擢拜陳州刺史。
units.en: (Ouyang Xiu's history, biography of Huangfu Hui: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Hui was raised from the ranks to prefect of Chenzhou.
units.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Huangfu Hui: When Mingzong took the throne, Hui was promoted from common soldier to Chenzhou prefect.

units.zh: 《九國誌·趙進傳》：天成初，除貝州刺史、鄴都衙內指揮使。）〉
units.en: Annals of the Nine States, biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Beizhou and commander of the Ye capital inner guard.)〉
units.literal: Annals of the Nine States, Biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng, he was made Beizhou prefect and Ye capital inner-palace army commander.)〉

units.zh: 在禮乃上表乞移旌節。
units.en: Zaili then memorialized, asking to be transferred to another post with full military commission.
units.literal: Zaili then submitted a memorial begging to be moved to another command with banners and staffs.

units.zh: 十二月，授滄州節度使。
units.en: In the twelfth month he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, he was appointed Cangzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 二年七月，移鎮兗州。
units.en: In the seventh month of the second year he was transferred to Yanzhou.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, he was transferred to garrison Yanzhou.

units.zh: 長興元年，入為左驍衛上將軍，俄改同州節度使。
units.en: In the first year of Changxing he was recalled to the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, and soon afterward was made military commissioner of Tongzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Changxing, he entered the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards; soon after he was changed to Tongzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 會高祖受明宗命統大軍伐蜀，以在禮充西川行營步軍都指揮使，收劍州而還。
units.en: When Gaozu received orders from Emperor Mingzong to command a great army against Shu, Zaili served as overall commander of the campaign's foot forces in the west, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.
units.literal: It happened that Gaozu received Mingzong's order to command a great army against Shu; Zaili was made overall commander of foot troops in the western Shu campaign headquarters, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.

units.zh: 四年，移鎮襄州。
units.en: In the fourth year he was transferred to Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to garrison Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 清泰三年，授宋州節度使，加檢校太尉、同平章事。
units.en: In the third year of Qingtai he was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou and given the additional titles of acting Grand Marshal and Grand Councillor.
units.literal: In the third year of Qingtai, he was appointed Songzhou military commissioner, with the added titles acting Grand Marshal and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 高祖登極，移鎮鄆州，加檢校太師、兼侍中，封衛國公。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zaili was transferred to Yunzhou, given the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaili was transferred to garrison Yunzhou, with the added titles acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

units.zh: 天福六年七月，授許州節度使。
units.en: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu, he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 八年四月，移鎮徐州，進封楚國公。
units.en: In the fourth month of the eighth year he was transferred to Xuzhou and advanced in rank to Duke of Chu.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chu.

units.zh: 開運元年，以契丹為患，少帝議北征。
units.en: In the first year of Kaiyun, with the Khitan posing a threat, the Young Emperor considered a northern campaign.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun, because the Khitan were a menace, the Young Emperor deliberated a northern expedition.

units.zh: 八月朔，降制命一十五將，以在禮為北面行營馬步都虞候。
units.en: On the first day of the eighth month, appointments were issued for fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign.
units.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, edicts were issued appointing fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot in the northern campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 十一月，改行營副都統，都虞候如故。
units.en: In the eleventh month he was made deputy overall commander of the campaign, while retaining his post as overall adjutant.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, he was changed to deputy overall commander of the campaign headquarters, remaining overall adjutant as before.

units.zh: 受詔屯澶州，再除兗州節度使，依前副都統。
units.en: Ordered to encamp at Chanzhou, he was again appointed military commissioner of Yanzhou while continuing as deputy overall commander.
units.literal: He received orders to station at Chanzhou, was again appointed Yanzhou military commissioner, and continued as deputy overall commander as before.

units.zh: 三年正月，授晉昌軍節度使。
units.en: In the first month of the third year he was appointed military commissioner of the Jinchang army.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year, he was appointed Jinchang army military commissioner.

units.zh: 時少帝為其子延煦娶在禮女為妻，禮會之日，其儀甚盛，京師以為榮觀。
units.en: The Young Emperor had his son Yanxu marry Zaili's daughter. On the wedding day the ceremonies were splendid, and the capital treated the event as a spectacle of honor.
units.literal: At that time the Young Emperor took Zaili's daughter as wife for his son Yanxu; on the day of the ceremonial meeting the rites were very grand, and the capital regarded it as an occasion of glory to behold.

units.zh: 五月，進封秦國公，累食邑至一萬三千戶，實封一千五百戶。
units.en: In the fifth month he was advanced to Duke of Qin, with cumulative fief households rising to thirteen thousand and actual fief households of one thousand five hundred.
units.literal: In the fifth month, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin; his cumulative fief households reached thirteen thousand, with one thousand five hundred actual fief households.

units.zh: 在禮歷十餘鎮，善治生殖貨，積財巨萬，兩京及所蒞藩鎮，皆邸店羅列。
units.en: Zaili served in more than ten commands and was skilled at managing productive commerce. He amassed immense wealth, and in both capitals and every garrison he held, shops and inns lined the streets.
units.literal: Zaili served in more than ten commands, skilled at managing productive commerce; he amassed wealth in the tens of thousands, and in both capitals and every garrison where he served, shops and inns lined the streets.

units.zh: 在宋州日，值天下飛蝗為害，在禮使比戶張幡幟，鳴鼙鼓，蝗皆越境而去，人亦服其智焉。
units.en: While he was at Songzhou, locusts plagued the realm. Zaili had every household raise banners and beat war drums, and the locusts all crossed the border and left. People admired his ingenuity.
units.literal: While at Songzhou, when locusts plagued the realm, Zaili had every household raise banners and flags and beat war drums; the locusts all crossed the border and departed, and people admired his cleverness.

units.zh: 凡聚斂所得，唯以奉權豪、崇釋氏而已。
units.en: Everything he gathered through exactions went only to serving the powerful and honoring Buddhism.
units.literal: All that he gathered through exactions he used only to serve the powerful and honor Buddhism.

units.zh: 及契丹入汴，自鎮赴闕，時契丹首領、奚王伊喇等在洛下，在禮望塵致敬，首領等倨受其禮，加之淩辱，邀索貨財，在禮不勝其憤。
units.en: When the Khitan entered Bian, Zaili came from his command to the capital. Khitan leaders, including the Xi king Yila, were then below Luoyang. Zaili bowed in respect from afar, but the leaders arrogantly received his courtesy, insulted him, and demanded goods and wealth until he could bear it no longer.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Zaili came from his command to the capital. At that time Khitan leaders, including the Xi king Yila, were below Luoyang. Zaili bowed in respect from afar, but the leaders arrogantly received his courtesy, added insult, and demanded goods and wealth; Zaili could not bear his anger.

units.zh: 行至鄭州，泊於逆旅，聞同州劉繼勛為契丹所鎖，大驚。
units.en: When he reached Zhengzhou and lodged at an inn, he heard that Liu Jixun of Tongzhou had been shackled by the Khitan and was greatly alarmed.
units.literal: When he reached Zhengzhou and lodged at an inn, he heard that Liu Jixun of Tongzhou had been shackled by the Khitan and was greatly alarmed.

units.zh: 丁未歲正月二十五日夜，以衣帶就馬櫪自絞而卒，年六十六。
units.en: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the first month in the dingwei year, he hanged himself with his belt from a horse manger and died at sixty-six.
units.literal: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the first month in the dingwei year, he hanged himself with his belt from a horse manger and died at age sixty-six.

units.zh: 漢高祖即位，贈中書令。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 在禮凡四子，雖歷內職，皆早卒。
units.en: Zaili had four sons in all; though they held posts at court, all died young.
units.literal: Zaili had four sons in all; although they held inner-court posts, all died young.

units.zh: 孫延勛，仕皇朝，歷嶽、蜀二州刺史。
units.en: His grandson Yanxun served the imperial court and held successive appointments as prefect of Yue and Shu.
units.literal: His grandson Yanxun served the imperial court and in succession was prefect of Yue and Shu prefectures.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：趙在禮之在宋州也，所為不法，百姓苦之。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: While Zhao Zaili was at Songzhou, his conduct was lawless and the people suffered under him.
units.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Zhao Zaili was at Songzhou, his conduct was unlawful and the common people suffered from it.

units.zh: 一旦下制移鎮永興，百姓欣然相賀，曰：「此人若去，可為眼中拔釘子，何快哉！」
units.en: One day an edict came transferring him to Yongxing. The people congratulated one another in delight, saying, "If this man leaves, it will be like pulling a nail from the eye—what relief!"
units.literal: One day an edict was issued transferring him to garrison Yongxing; the common people gladly congratulated one another, saying, "If this man goes, it will be like pulling a nail from the eye—how delightful!"

units.zh: 在禮聞之怒，欲報「拔釘」之謗，遽上表更求宋州一年，時朝廷姑息勛臣，詔許之。
units.en: When Zaili heard of this he was furious and wished to punish the "nail-pulling" talk. He hastily memorialized asking to remain at Songzhou for one more year. The court, indulgent toward meritorious ministers, granted his request.
units.literal: Zaili heard of it and was angry, wishing to retaliate for the slander of "pulling the nail"; he hastily submitted a memorial asking instead for one more year at Songzhou. At that time the court indulged meritorious ministers, and an edict granted it.

units.zh: 在禮於是命吏籍管內戶口，不論主客，每歲一千，納之於家，號曰「拔釘錢」，莫不公行督責，有不如約，則加之鞭樸，雖租賦之不若也。
units.en: Zaili then ordered clerks to register every household in his jurisdiction, native or migrant alike, and exact one thousand cash per year for his private purse, calling it "nail-pulling money." Collection was enforced openly; anyone who fell short was beaten with whip and cudgel—harsher than ordinary taxes.
units.literal: Zaili thereupon ordered clerks to register households within his jurisdiction, whether native or guest, one thousand per year paid into his household, called "nail-pulling money"; none failed to be openly compelled and exacted, and if they did not meet the agreement, they were given the whip and cudgel—even worse than land tax and levies.

units.zh: 是歲獲錢百萬。）〉
units.en: That year he took in a million in cash.)〉
units.literal: That year he obtained a million in cash.)〉

units.zh: 馬全節，字大雅，魏郡元城人也。
units.en: Ma Quanjie, courtesy name Daya, was a native of Yuancheng in Weijun.
units.literal: Ma Quanjie, style name Daya, was a man of Yuancheng in Weijun.

units.zh: 父文操，本府軍校，官至檢校尚書左僕射，以全節之貴，累贈太師。
units.en: His father Wencao was a military officer of the native command, rising to acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; because of Quanjie's eminence, he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: His father Wencao was a military officer of the native prefecture, reaching the post of acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; because of Quanjie's eminence, he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 全節少從軍旅，同光末，為捉生指揮使。
units.en: Quanjie entered the army in his youth. At the end of the Tongguang era he was commander of the captive-taking corps.
units.literal: Quanjie in youth followed the army; at the end of Tongguang he was commander of the captive-taking corps.

units.zh: 趙在禮之據魏州也，為鄴都馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili held Weizhou, Quanjie served as overall commander of the Ye capital's horse and foot forces.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili held Weizhou, he was overall commander of horse and foot in the Ye capital.

units.zh: 唐明宗即位，授檢校司空，歷博、單二州刺史。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang took the throne, Quanjie was appointed acting Minister of Works and served in succession as prefect of Bo and Shan.
units.literal: When Tang Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was appointed acting Minister of Works and in succession was prefect of Bo and Shan prefectures.

units.zh: 天成三年，賜竭忠建策興復功臣，移刺郢州。
units.en: In the third year of Tiancheng he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Devises Plans, and Restores the Dynasty, and was transferred to Yingzhou.
units.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng, he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Devises Plans, and Restores the Dynasty, and was transferred to govern Yingzhou.

units.zh: 長興初，就加檢校司徒，在郡有政聲，俄授河西節度使。
units.en: At the beginning of Changxing he was further made acting Minister of Education. He earned a reputation for good government in his prefecture and was soon appointed military commissioner of Hexi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, he was further given the title acting Minister of Education; while in the prefecture he had a reputation for good government, and soon was appointed Hexi military commissioner.

units.zh: 時明宗命高祖伐蜀，師次岐山，全節赴任及之，具軍容謁於轅門，高祖以地理隔越，乃奏還焉，移沂州刺史。
units.en: Emperor Mingzong had ordered Gaozu to campaign against Shu, and the army halted at Qishan. Quanjie arrived to take up his new post and presented himself in full military dress at the camp gate. Gaozu, finding the region too remote, memorialized to have him recalled and transferred him to prefect of Yizhou.
units.literal: At that time Mingzong ordered Gaozu to attack Shu; the army halted at Qishan. Quanjie went to take up his post and reached them, fully arrayed in military dress paying respects at the camp gate. Gaozu, because the geography was remote and cut off, memorialized to have him returned and transferred him to Yizhou prefect.

units.zh: 清泰初，為金州防禦使。
units.en: At the beginning of Qingtai he was defense commissioner of Jinzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, he was Jinzhou defense commissioner.

units.zh: 會蜀軍攻其城，州兵才千人，兵馬都監陳知隱懼，托以他事出城，領三百人順流而逸，賊既盛，人情憂沮。
units.en: When Shu forces attacked his city, the prefectural garrison numbered only a thousand. The horse-and-foot supervisory commissioner Chen Zhiyin, in fear, left the city on a pretext and fled downstream with three hundred men. With the enemy strong, morale collapsed.
units.literal: It happened that Shu troops attacked his city; the prefectural army numbered only a thousand. The horse-and-foot supervisory commissioner Chen Zhiyin was afraid, used some other matter as pretext to leave the city, and led three hundred men downstream in flight. The bandits were already strong, and popular sentiment was anxious and dejected.

units.zh: 全節乃悉家財以給士，復出奇拒戰，以死繼之。
units.en: Quanjie then spent his entire household fortune to supply the troops, led surprise attacks against the enemy, and fought on through repeated casualties.
units.literal: Quanjie then exhausted his household wealth to supply the soldiers, again deployed surprise forces to resist in battle, and followed one death with another.

units.zh: 賊退，朝廷嘉其功，詔赴闕，將議賞典。
units.en: When the enemy withdrew, the court praised his achievement and summoned him to the capital to consider his reward.
units.literal: The bandits retreated; the court praised his achievement and ordered him to come to the capital, intending to deliberate rewards.

units.zh: 時劉延朗為樞密副使，邀其厚賄，全節無以賂之，謂全節曰：「絳州闕人，請事行計。」
units.en: Liu Yanlang was then Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and demanded a heavy bribe. Quanjie had nothing to give him. Yanlang told Quanjie, "Jiangzhou lacks a commander—make your travel plans accordingly."
units.literal: At that time Liu Yanlang was Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he demanded a heavy bribe. Quanjie had nothing with which to bribe him. He said to Quanjie, "Jiangzhou lacks a man—please attend to travel arrangements."

units.zh: 全節不樂，告其同輩，由是眾口喧然，以為不當，皇子重美為河南尹，聞而奏焉。
units.en: Quanjie was displeased and told his colleagues, and word spread that the appointment was improper. Prince Chongmei, serving as Henan Intendant, heard of it and memorialized the throne.
units.literal: Quanjie was displeased and told his colleagues; thereby many mouths clamored that it was improper. The prince Chongmei was Henan Intendant; hearing of it, he memorialized.

units.zh: 清泰帝召全節謂曰：「滄州乏帥，欲命卿制置。」
units.en: Emperor Qingtai summoned Quanjie and said, "Cangzhou lacks a commander. I intend to put you in charge there."
units.literal: Emperor Qingtai summoned Quanjie and said, "Cangzhou lacks a commander; I wish to order you to take charge."

units.zh: 翌日，授橫海軍兩使留後。
units.en: The next day he was appointed acting commissioner of the Henghai army.
units.literal: The next day he was appointed acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs for the Henghai army.

units.zh: 高祖即位，加檢校太保，正授旌節。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Quanjie was given the added title of acting Grand Guardian and received a full military commission.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was given the added title acting Grand Guardian and was formally granted banners and staffs.

units.zh: 天福五年，授檢校太傅，移鎮安州。
units.en: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed acting Grand Tutor and transferred to Anzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, he was appointed acting Grand Tutor and transferred to garrison Anzhou.

units.zh: 時李金全據州叛，引淮軍為援，因命全節將兵討平之，以功加檢校太尉，改昭義軍節度、澤潞遼沁等州觀察處置等使。
units.en: When Li Jinquan rebelled and held the prefecture, bringing Huai troops as reinforcements, Quanjie was ordered to lead an army against him and restore order. For this service he was made acting Grand Marshal and military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, with oversight of Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and related prefectures.
units.literal: At that time Li Jinquan held the prefecture in rebellion and brought Huai troops as reinforcements; he was therefore ordered to lead troops to suppress and pacify it. For his merit he was given the added title acting Grand Marshal and was changed to Zhaoyi army military commissioner and overseer and disposition commissioner for Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 六年秋，移鎮邢州，加同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he was transferred to Xingzhou and made Grand Councillor with Secretariat precedence.
units.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year, he was transferred to garrison Xingzhou and given the added title Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery with the same precedence as the Secretariat.

units.zh: 安重榮之叛也，授鎮州行營副招討兼排陣使，與重榮戰於宋城，大敗之。
units.en: When An Chongrong rebelled, Quanjie was appointed deputy commander of the Zhenzhou suppression force and array marshal. He met Chongrong at Songcheng and routed him.
units.literal: When An Chongrong rebelled, he was appointed deputy commander for suppression in the Zhenzhou campaign headquarters and concurrently array marshal; he fought Chongrong at Songcheng and inflicted a great defeat.

units.zh: 鎮州平，加開府儀同三司，充義武軍節度、易定祁等州觀察處置、北平軍等使。
units.en: After Zhenzhou was pacified, he was given the rank of Palace Captain with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and appointed military commissioner of the Yiwu army, with oversight of Yi, Ding, Qi, and related prefectures and command of the Northern Pacification army.
units.literal: When Zhenzhou was pacified, he was given the added title Palace Captain with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and made Yiwu army military commissioner, overseer and disposition commissioner for Yi, Ding, Qi, and other prefectures, and commissioner of the Northern Pacification army and related posts.

units.zh: 八年秋，丁母憂，尋起復焉。
units.en: In the autumn of the eighth year he entered mourning for his mother, but was soon recalled to office.
units.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, he entered mourning for his mother; soon he was recalled from mourning.

units.zh: 屬契丹侵寇，加之蝗旱，國家有所征發，全節朝受命而夕行，治生餘財，必充貢奉。
units.en: With Khitan raids and locust plague and drought afflicting the realm, whenever the court issued a call, Quanjie would receive orders in the morning and march by evening. Any surplus from his private affairs he turned over as tribute.
units.literal: It fell at a time when the Khitan invaded and raided, and locusts and drought were added; whenever the state had requisitions, Quanjie received orders in the morning and marched by evening; whatever surplus he had from managing livelihood, he invariably devoted to tribute and offerings.

units.zh: 開運元年秋，授鄴都留守、檢校太師、兼侍中、廣晉尹、幽州道行營馬步軍都虞候，尋加天雄軍北面行營副招討使，陽城之戰，甚有力焉。
units.en: In the autumn of the first year of Kaiyun he was appointed garrison commander of the Ye capital, acting Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, Guangjin Intendant, and overall adjutant of horse and foot on the Youzhou campaign. Soon afterward he was made deputy commander of the Tianxiong army's northern suppression force. At the battle of Yangcheng he distinguished himself greatly.
units.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Kaiyun, he was appointed Ye capital garrison commander, acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, Guangjin Intendant, and overall adjutant of horse and foot on the Youzhou circuit campaign; soon he was given the added post of deputy commander for suppression in the Tianxiong army's northern campaign headquarters. In the battle of Yangcheng he contributed greatly.

units.zh: 全節始拜鄴都，以元城是桑梓之邑，具白襕詣縣庭謁拜，縣令沈遘逡巡避之，不敢當禮。
units.en: When Quanjie first took office at the Ye capital, he went in white robes to the county court of Yuancheng, his home district, to pay his respects. The magistrate Shen Gou drew back in embarrassment and would not accept the gesture.
units.literal: When Quanjie first took the Ye capital post, because Yuancheng was his native district he put on white robes and went to the county court to pay respects; the county magistrate Shen Gou hesitated and avoided him, not daring to receive the courtesy.

units.zh: 全節曰：「父母之鄉，自合致敬，勿讓之也。」
units.en: Quanjie said, "This is the home of my parents. It is only right that I show respect—do not refuse me."
units.literal: Quanjie said, "The village of one's parents—one ought by rights to show respect; do not decline it."

units.zh: 州裏榮之。
units.en: The people of the district were proud of the gesture.
units.literal: The district took it as an honor.

units.zh: 二年，授順國軍節度使，未赴鎮卒，年五十五。
units.en: In the second year he was appointed military commissioner of the Shunguo army, but died before he could take up the post, at the age of fifty-five.
units.literal: In the second year, he was appointed Shunguo army military commissioner; before he could go to take up the garrison he died, aged fifty-five.

units.zh: 贈中書令。
units.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 全節事母王氏至孝，位歷方鎮，溫清面告，畢盡其敬。
units.en: Quanjie was deeply filial toward his mother, Lady Wang. Though he held successive regional commands, he still attended to her comfort in person and showed her every respect.
units.literal: Quanjie served his mother Lady Wang with utmost filial piety; though his posts spanned regional commands, he attended to her warmth and comfort in person and fully exhausted his reverence.

units.zh: 政事動與幕客謀議，故鮮有敗事。
units.en: He routinely consulted his staff on affairs of government, and therefore rarely failed in his undertakings.
units.literal: In government affairs he invariably deliberated with staff officers, and therefore rarely had failed undertakings.

units.zh: 鎮中山日，杜威為恒州，方奏括境內民家粟，時軍吏引恒州例，堅請行之，全節曰：「邊民遇蝗旱，而家食方困，官司復擾之，則不堪其命矣。
units.en: While he was stationed at Zhongshan, Du Wei governed Hengzhou and had memorialized to seize grain from households within his jurisdiction. Quanjie's military staff cited the Hengzhou precedent and pressed to do the same. Quanjie said, "The border people have suffered locust plague and drought, and household stores are already exhausted. If the authorities harass them further, they cannot endure it.
units.literal: While he garrisoned Zhongshan, Du Wei was at Hengzhou and had just memorialized to seize grain from households within the jurisdiction. At that time military clerks cited the Hengzhou precedent and firmly requested to carry it out. Quanjie said, "The border people have encountered locusts and drought, and household food is already in distress; if the authorities again harass them, they cannot bear such a fate.

units.zh: 我為廉察，安忍效尤。」
units.en: As overseer, how could I copy such an example?"
units.literal: I serve as overseer and inspector—how can I bear to follow a bad example?"

units.zh: 百姓稱其德。
units.en: The people praised his virtue.
units.literal: The common people praised his virtue.

units.zh: 先是，全節自上黨攜歌妓一人之中山，館於外舍，有人以讒言中之，全節害之。
units.en: Earlier, Quanjie had brought a song-girl from Shangdang to Zhongshan and lodged her in an outer residence. When someone slandered him over the affair, he had her killed.
units.literal: Earlier, Quanjie had brought one song-girl from Shangdang to Zhongshan and lodged her in an outer residence; someone struck at him with slanderous words, and Quanjie killed her.

units.zh: 及詔除恒陽，遇疾，數見其妓，厭之復來。
units.en: When he was ordered to Hengyang, he fell ill and repeatedly saw the girl. He loathed her return.
units.literal: When an edict removed him to Hengyang, he fell ill and repeatedly saw the song-girl; he detested her coming again.

units.zh: 妓曰：「我已得請，要公俱行。」
units.en: The girl said, "I have already obtained leave. You must come with me."
units.literal: The girl said, "I have already obtained permission—I require you to go together."

units.zh: 全節具告家人，數日而卒。
units.en: Quanjie told his family everything. Within days he was dead.
units.literal: Quanjie fully told his family; within several days he died.

units.zh: 子令威，歷隰、陳、懷三州刺史，卒。
units.en: His son Lingwei served in succession as prefect of Xi, Chen, and Huai, and died in office.
units.literal: His son Lingwei in succession was prefect of Xi, Chen, and Huai prefectures and died.

units.zh: 張筠，海州人也。
units.en: Zhang Yun was a native of Haizhou.
units.literal: Zhang Yun, was a man of Haizhou.

units.zh: 父傳古，世為郡之大商，唐乾符末，屬江淮俶擾，遂徙家彭門。
units.en: His father Chuangu had for generations been one of the prefecture's great merchants. At the end of the Tang Qianfu era, with the Jiang-Huai region in turmoil, he moved the family to Pengmen.
units.literal: His father Chuangu was for generations a great merchant of the prefecture; at the end of the Qianfu era of Tang, because the Jiang-Huai region was in turmoil, he moved his household to Pengmen.

units.zh: 時彭門連帥時溥為東南面招討使，據有數郡之地，擢筠為偏將，累有軍功，奏授宿州刺史。
units.en: The Pengmen commander Shi Pu was then southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures. He promoted Yun to deputy general; Yun won repeated military distinction, and Pu memorialized to have him appointed prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: At that time the Pengmen commander Shi Pu was southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures' territory; he promoted Yun to deputy general, who repeatedly had military merit, and memorialized to appoint him Suzhou prefect.

units.zh: 後溥與梁祖不協，梁人進攻宿州，下之，獲筠以歸。
units.en: Later, when Pu fell out with the Liang founder, Liang forces attacked Suzhou, captured it, and took Yun back with them.
units.literal: Later Pu was at odds with the Liang founder; Liang men advanced to attack Suzhou, took it, and captured Yun to bring back.

units.zh: 梁方圖霸業，以筠言貌辯秀，命為四鎮客將，久之，轉長直軍使。
units.en: With Liang then plotting supremacy, Yun's eloquence and polished appearance won him appointment as guest general of the four commands. After a long interval he was made chief of the long-duty army.
units.literal: Liang was then plotting hegemony; because Yun's speech and appearance were eloquent and refined, he was ordered to be a guest general of the four commands; after a long time he was transferred to chief of the long-duty army.

units.zh: 梁唐革命，遷右龍武統軍，歷客省使、宣徽使，出為復、商二州刺史，復為宣徽使。
units.en: When Liang gave way to Tang, Yun was transferred to commander of the Right Valiant Dragons, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, was sent out as prefect of Fu and Shang, and again became palace treasury commissioner.
units.literal: When Liang underwent the Tang revolution, he was transferred to Right Valiant Dragon commander, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, went out as prefect of Fu and Shang prefectures, and again became palace treasury commissioner.

units.zh: 梁室割相、衛為昭德軍，命筠為兩使留後。
units.en: The Liang court carved out Xiang and Wei as the Zhaode army and appointed Yun acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.
units.literal: The Liang house carved Xiang and Wei into the Zhaode army and ordered Yun as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.

units.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，筠委城南歸，授右衛上將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and submitted, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.
units.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and returned, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.

units.zh: 會雍州康懷英以病告，詔筠往代之，比至，懷英已卒，因除筠為永平軍節度使、大安尹。
units.en: When Kang Huaiying of Yongzhou reported illness, Yun was ordered to replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying was already dead, and Yun was appointed military commissioner of the Yongping army and Intendant of Da'an.
units.literal: It happened that Yongzhou's Kang Huaiying reported illness; an edict ordered Yun to go replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying had already died, and Yun was therefore appointed Yongping army military commissioner and Da'an Intendant.

units.zh: 懷英在長安日，家財甚厚，筠盡奪之，復於大內掘地，繼獲金玉。
units.en: Huaiying had amassed great wealth while at Chang'an; Yun seized it all. He also dug within the inner palace grounds and unearthed gold and jade.
units.literal: When Huaiying was at Chang'an, his household wealth was very great; Yun seized it all. Again within the great inner palace he dug the ground and subsequently obtained gold and jade.

units.zh: 時有涇陽鎮將侯莫威，前與溫韜同剽唐氏諸陵，大貯瑰異之物，筠乃殺威而籍其家，遂蓄積巨萬。
units.en: The Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei had earlier joined Wen Tao in plundering the tombs of the Tang imperial house and hoarded extraordinary treasures. Yun killed him and confiscated his property, amassing wealth in the tens of thousands.
units.literal: At that time there was Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei, who earlier with Wen Tao together plundered the tombs of the Tang house and greatly stored rare and wondrous objects; Yun then killed Wei and registered his household, thereby amassing tens of thousands.

units.zh: 然性好施，每出遇貧民於路，則給與口食衣物，境內除省賦外，未嘗聚斂，遂致百姓不撓，十年小康，秦民懷惠，呼為「佛子」。
units.en: Yet he was generous by nature: whenever he went out and met the poor on the road, he gave them food and clothing. Apart from provincial levies, he never extorted within his jurisdiction, and the people were left unmolested. For ten years the region knew modest prosperity; the people of Qin were grateful and called him "the Buddha's son."
units.literal: Yet his nature was fond of giving; whenever he went out and met poor people on the road, he supplied them food and clothing. Within his jurisdiction, apart from provincial levies, he never amassed and exacted, and thereby caused the common people not to be harassed; for ten years there was modest prosperity, and the Qin people cherished his kindness, calling him "Buddha's Son."

units.zh: 同光中，從郭崇韜為劍南安撫使，蜀平歸洛，權領河南尹，俄鎮興元，所治之地，上下安之。
units.en: During the Tongguang era he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner. After Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, served provisionally as Henan Intendant, and soon took up command at Xingyuan, where high and low alike lived in peace under his rule.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era, he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner; when Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, provisionally headed Henan as Intendant, and soon garrisoned Xingyuan—the places he governed, high and low were at peace.

units.zh: 筠時有疾，軍州官吏久不得見，副使符彥琳等面請問疾，筠又不諾，彥琳等疑其已死，慮左右有謀，遂請權交牌印，筠命左右收彥琳下獄，以叛聞。
units.en: Yun was then ill, and the military and civil officials had long been unable to see him. Deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others came in person to inquire after his health, but Yun refused them again. Yanlin and the others suspected he was already dead and feared a plot among his attendants; they asked to take custody of the seals provisionally. Yun ordered his attendants to arrest Yanlin and imprison him, then reported him for rebellion.
units.literal: Yun at that time had illness; the army and prefecture officials for a long time could not see him. The deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others in person requested to inquire after his illness; Yun again did not assent. Yanlin and others suspected he was already dead and feared that those around him had designs; they therefore requested to hand over the tally and seal provisionally. Yun ordered those around him to seize Yanlin and put him in prison, reporting rebellion.

units.zh: 詔取彥琳等至洛，釋而不問，因授筠西京留守，誘離興元。
units.en: An edict summoned Yanlin and the others to Luoyang and released them without punishment. Yun was then appointed garrison commander of the western capital, a move intended to draw him away from Xingyuan.
units.literal: An edict took Yanlin and others to Luoyang, released them without inquiry, and thereby appointed Yun western capital garrison commander to lure him away from Xingyuan.

units.zh: 及至長安，守兵閉門不納，筠東朝於洛，詔遣歸第。
units.en: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison closed the gates and refused him entry. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang, where an edict sent him back to his private residence.
units.literal: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison troops closed the gates and would not admit him. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang; an edict sent him back to his residence.

units.zh: 筠前為京兆尹，奉詔殺偽蜀主王衍，衍之妓樂寶貨，悉私藏於家。
units.en: Yun had earlier served as Intendant of Jingzhao and, by imperial order, executed the puppet Shu ruler Wang Yan; he then secretly kept at home all of Yan's performers, music, and valuables.
units.literal: Previously, when Yun had been Intendant of Jingzhao, he received an edict to execute the false Shu ruler Wang Yan; Yan's entertainers, music, and treasures he secretly hoarded entirely at home.

units.zh: 及罷歸之後，第宅宏敞，花竹深邃，聲樂飲膳，恣其所欲，十年之內，人謂「地仙」。
units.en: After he retired and returned home, his mansion was grand and spacious, with deep groves of flowers and bamboo; music and feasting were at his pleasure. Within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."
units.literal: When he returned after leaving office, his residence was vast and spacious, flowers and bamboo deep and secluded, music and feasting as he wished; within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."

units.zh: 天福二年，上表乞歸長安，俄而洛下張從賓之亂，筠獨免其難，人咸謂筠有五福之具美焉。
units.en: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon afterward Zhang Congbin's rebellion erupted in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped harm, and all agreed that he truly enjoyed the full measure of the five blessings.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon Zhang Congbin's rebellion broke out in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped the calamity, and everyone said Yun truly possessed the full beauty of the five blessings.

units.zh: 是歲，卒於家。
units.en: That year he died at home.
units.literal: That year he died at home.

units.zh: 贈太子太師。
units.en: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 弟篯。
units.en: Younger brother Jian.
units.literal: Younger brother Jian.

units.zh: 篯，字慕彭，少嗜酒無節，為鄉里所鄙。
units.en: Jian, courtesy name Mupeng, was in his youth addicted to wine without restraint and was despised in his home district.
units.literal: Jian, style name Mupeng, in youth was addicted to wine without restraint and was despised by his district.

units.zh: 唐天復中，兄筠為大梁四鎮客將，篯自海州省兄，兄薦於兗州連帥王瓚，用為裨校。
units.en: During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun served as guest general of Daliang's four commands. Jian traveled from Haizhou to visit him; Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who took him on as adjutant.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun was guest general of the four commands of Daliang; Jian came from Haizhou to visit his brother, and Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who employed him as adjutant.

units.zh: 篯性桀黠，善事人，累遷軍職。
units.en: Jian was clever and crafty by nature, adept at winning people over, and rose repeatedly through military ranks.
units.literal: Jian's nature was clever and crafty; he was skilled at pleasing people and was repeatedly promoted in military posts.

units.zh: 後唐莊宗都洛，筠鎮長安，自衙內指揮使授檢校司空、右千牛衛將軍同正，領饒州刺史、西京管內三白渠營田制置使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang established his capital at Luoyang, Yun garrisoned Chang'an. From palace-inner commander he was made acting Minister of Works and Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently served as prefect of Raozhou and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration in the western capital circuit.
units.literal: When Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, Yun garrisoned Chang'an; from palace-inner commander he was appointed acting Minister of Works, Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently Raozhou prefect and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration within the western capital circuit.

units.zh: 同光末，筠隨魏王繼岌伐蜀，奏篯權知西京留守事。
units.en: At the end of the Tongguang era Yun followed the Prince of Wei, Li Jiji, on the campaign against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally handle western capital garrison affairs.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang, Yun followed the Prince of Wei Li Jiji in the expedition against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally administer western capital garrison affairs.

units.zh: 蜀平，王衍挈族入朝，至秦川驛，莊宗遣中使向延嗣乘驛騎盡戮王衍之族，所有奇貨，盡歸於延嗣。
units.en: After Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent the palace envoy Xiang Yansi on relay horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods went entirely to Yansi.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent palace envoy Xiang Yansi on post-horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods fell entirely to Yansi.

units.zh: 俄聞莊宗遇內難，繼岌軍次興平，篯乃斷咸陽浮橋，繼岌浮渡至渭南死之，一行金寶妓樂，篯悉獲之。
units.en: Soon word arrived that Zhuangzong had met with internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian cut the Xianyang floating bridge, and Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan, where he died. Jian seized the whole train of gold, jewels, and entertainers.
units.literal: Soon word came that Zhuangzong had met internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian severed the Xianyang floating bridge, Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan and died there; the entire train of gold, jewels, and entertainers Jian seized entirely.

units.zh: 俄而明宗使人誅延嗣，延嗣暗遁，
units.en: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,
units.literal: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：明宗即位，忿閹豎輩怙勢擅權，先敕使四方及此遁不出者，皆擒戮之，死者殆盡。）〉
units.en: (Annals of the Nine States records: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, enraged at the eunuchs who relied on power and monopolized authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys throughout the realm and those in hiding who did not come forth be seized and executed; nearly all were killed.)〉
units.literal: (Annals of the Nine States: When Mingzong took the throne, angry at the eunuch faction that relied on power and usurped authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys sent to the four directions and those who had fled and did not emerge be captured and executed; nearly all died.)〉

units.zh: 衍之行裝復為篯有，因為富家，積白金萬鎰，藏於窟室。
units.en: Wang Yan's traveling goods again fell into Jian's hands; he thus became a wealthy man, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver in a hidden vault.
units.literal: Wang Yan's traveling goods again became Jian's possession; he thus became a wealthy house, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver stored in a hidden vault.

units.zh: 明宗即位，篯進王衍犀、玉帶各二，馬一百五十匹，魏王打球馬七十匹，旋除沂州刺史，入為西衛將軍。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros-horn belts and two jade belts from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy of the Prince of Wei's polo horses; he was soon made prefect of Yizhou and then appointed general of the western guards.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros and jade belts each from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy polo horses of the Prince of Wei; he was soon appointed Yizhou prefect and entered service as western guards general.

units.zh: 高祖即位之明年，加檢校太保，出典密州，未幾，復居環衛。
units.en: In the year after Gaozu's accession he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and before long returned to the palace guards.
units.literal: The year after Gaozu ascended, he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and soon after returned to the palace guards.

units.zh: 時湖南馬希範與篯有舊，奏朝廷請命篯為使，允之。
units.en: At that time Ma Xifan of Hunan was an old acquaintance of Jian's and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; the request was granted.
units.literal: At that time Hunan's Ma Xifan was old friends with Jian and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; approval was granted.

units.zh: 篯密賫蜀之奇貨往售，又獲十餘萬緡以歸。
units.en: Jian secretly took Shu's rare goods to sell and returned with more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.
units.literal: Jian secretly carried Shu rare goods to sell and returned having gained more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.

units.zh: 篯出入以庖者十餘人從行，食皆水陸之珍鮮，厚自奉養，無與為比。
units.en: Whenever Jian went out, more than ten cooks attended him; his meals were delicacies from land and sea. He lived in unrivaled luxury.
units.literal: When going out, Jian was attended by more than ten cooks; his food was delicacies from land and sea; he maintained himself lavishly, unmatched by any other.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，詔遣往西蕃，及回，以其馬劣，為有司所糾，復當路有不足者，遂有詔征其舊價。
units.en: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return his horses were judged inferior and the authorities impeached him; moreover those in power who disliked him secured an edict to recover the original purchase price.
units.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return, because his horses were inferior, he was impeached by the authorities; furthermore there were those in power who bore him ill will, and an edict was issued to collect the old purchase price.

units.zh: 篯上言請貨故京田業，許之，因憤惋成疾而卒。
units.en: Jian memorialized asking to mortgage his former estates in the capital; permission was granted, but indignation and distress brought on illness and he died.
units.literal: Jian memorialized asking to pawn his former capital estates; permission was granted, but resentment and distress brought on illness and he died.

units.zh: 篯始在雍州，因春景舒和，出遊近郊，憩於大冢之上，忽有黃雀銜一銅錢置於前而去。
units.en: When Jian was first at Yongzhou, in the mild spring weather he went out to the near suburbs and rested atop a great mound. Suddenly a yellow finch placed a copper coin before him and flew away.
units.literal: When Jian was first at Yongzhou, taking advantage of gentle spring weather, he went out to tour the near suburbs and rested atop a great tumulus. Suddenly a yellow finch placed a copper coin before him and flew away.

units.zh: 未幾，復於衙院晝臥，見二燕相鬥畢，各銜一錢落於篯首。
units.en: Before long, while napping by day in the yamen courtyard, he saw two swallows finish fighting; each dropped a coin onto Jian's head.
units.literal: Before long, while napping by day in the yamen courtyard, he saw two swallows finish fighting; each carried a coin that fell onto Jian's head.

units.zh: 前後所獲三錢，嘗秘於巾箱，識者以為大富之征。
units.en: The three coins he had received were kept secret in a cloth casket; those versed in omens took this as a sign of great wealth.
units.literal: The three coins obtained before and after were kept secret in a cloth casket; those who knew augury took this as a sign of great wealth.

units.zh: 其後家雖厚積，性實鄙吝，未嘗與士大夫遊處。
units.en: Though his household later grew very rich, he was by nature mean and stingy and never kept company with scholar-officials.
units.literal: Though his household later amassed great wealth, his nature was truly mean and stingy; he never associated with scholar-officials.

units.zh: 及令市馬，利在私門，不省咎以輸其直，郁郁致死，愚之甚耶！
units.en: When ordered to supply horses, he kept the profit for himself and would not accept blame by paying the full price; he died in sullen distress—was his folly not extreme!
units.literal: When ordered to supply horses, he kept the profit for himself and would not bear guilt by paying the full price, dying sullenly from distress—was his folly not extreme!

units.zh: 華溫琪，字德潤，宋州下邑人也。
units.en: Hua Wenqi, courtesy name Derun, was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou.
units.literal: Hua Wenqi, style name Derun, was a man of Xiayi in Songzhou.

units.zh: 祖楚，以農為業。
units.en: His grandfather Chu made his living as a farmer.
units.literal: His grandfather Chu made his living by farming.

units.zh: 父敬忠，後以溫琪貴，官至檢校尚書。
units.en: His father Jingzhong later, through Wenqi's eminence, rose to acting Minister.
units.literal: His father Jingzhong later, through Wenqi's eminence, reached the post of acting Minister.

units.zh: 溫琪長七尺餘，唐廣明中，從黃巢為紀綱，巢陷長安，偽署溫琪為供奉都知。
units.en: Wenqi stood more than seven feet tall. In the Tang Guangming era he followed Huang Chao as enforcer; when Chao seized Chang'an he falsely appointed Wenqi director of imperial attendance.
units.literal: Wenqi stood over seven feet. In the Tang Guangming era he followed Huang Chao as enforcer; when Chao took Chang'an, he falsely appointed Wenqi director of imperial attendance.

units.zh: 巢敗，奔至滑臺，以形貌魁岸，懼不自容，乃投白馬河下流，俄而浮至淺處，會行人救免；
units.en: When Chao was defeated, Wenqi fled to Huatai. His imposing build made him fear he could not remain hidden; he threw himself into the lower reaches of the Baima River, soon floated to shallows, and was saved by passersby;
units.literal: When Chao was defeated, Wenqi fled to Huatai. His imposing stature made him fear he could not hide; he threw himself into the lower reaches of the Baima River, soon floated to shallows, and passersby saved him;

units.zh: 又登桑自經，枝折墜地，不死。
units.en: He climbed a mulberry to hang himself; the branch broke and he fell to the ground, yet did not die.
units.literal: He climbed a mulberry to hang himself; the branch broke and he fell to earth, yet did not die.

units.zh: 夜至胙縣界，有田父見溫琪非常人，遂匿於家。
units.en: By night he reached the border of Zuo County; a farmer saw that Wenqi was no ordinary man and hid him in his home.
units.literal: By night he reached the border of Zuo County; a farmer saw that Wenqi was no ordinary man and hid him at home.

units.zh: 經歲餘，會梁將朱友裕為濮州刺史，召募勇士，溫琪往依之，友裕署為小校，漸升為馬軍都將。
units.en: After more than a year, the Liang general Zhu Youyu became prefect of Puzhou and recruited braves; Wenqi went to join him. Youyu appointed him junior officer, and he gradually rose to commander of the horse army.
units.literal: After more than a year, Liang general Zhu Youyu became Puzhou prefect and recruited braves; Wenqi went to join him. Youyu appointed him junior officer, and he gradually rose to horse-army commander.

units.zh: 從友裕擊秦宗權於曹南，有功，奏加檢校太子賓客，梁祖擢為開道指揮使，加檢校工部尚書，出屯鄜畤。
units.en: Following Youyu he attacked Qin Zongquan in southern Cao with distinction; he was memorialized for acting Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent; the Liang founder promoted him to Kaizhou road commander and acting Minister of Works and stationed him at Meizhi.
units.literal: Following Youyu he attacked Qin Zongquan at the southern Cao region with merit; memorialized for acting Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent; the Liang founder promoted him to Kaizhou road commander, acting Minister of Works, and garrisoned him at Meizhi.

units.zh: 會延州胡璋叛命，來寇郡境，溫琪擊退之。
units.en: When Hu Zhang of Yanzhou rebelled and raided the prefectural borders, Wenqi drove him back.
units.literal: When Yanzhou's Hu Zhang rebelled and came to raid the prefectural borders, Wenqi repelled him.

units.zh: 尋奉詔營長安，以功遷絳州刺史。
units.en: Soon he received orders to rebuild Chang'an; for this merit he was transferred to prefect of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Soon he received orders to build up Chang'an; for this merit he was transferred to Jiangzhou prefect.

units.zh: 歲餘，刺棣州。
units.en: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Dizhou.
units.literal: After more than a year he was made prefect of Dizhou.

units.zh: 溫琪以州城每年為河水所壞，居人不堪其苦，表請移於便地，朝廷許之。
units.en: Wenqi saw that each year the prefectural city was ruined by the river and the people could not endure the hardship; he memorialized to relocate to a more suitable site, and the court approved.
units.literal: Wenqi observed that each year the prefectural city was destroyed by river water and the inhabitants could not bear the suffering; he memorialized to move to a convenient site, and the court approved.

units.zh: 板築既畢，賜立紀功碑，仍加檢校尚書左僕射，繼遷齊州、晉州節度使。
units.en: When the fortifications were complete, a merit stele was erected in his honor; he was further made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and later served in succession as military commissioner of Qizhou and Jinzhou.
units.literal: When the wall-building was finished, he was granted a merit stele; additionally made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thereafter transferred in succession as military commissioner of Qizhou and Jinzhou.

units.zh: 溫琪在平陽日，唐莊宗嘗引兵攻之，逾月不下，梁人賞之，升晉州為定昌軍，以溫琪為節度使，加檢校太保。
units.en: While Wenqi was at Pingyang, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang once led troops against him; for more than a month he could not take the city. The Liang court rewarded him by elevating Jinzhou to the Dingchang army, appointing Wenqi its military commissioner, and adding the title acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: During Wenqi's days at Pingyang, Tang Emperor Zhuangzong once led troops to attack him; for more than a month he could not take it; the Liang court rewarded him, elevated Jinzhou to the Dingchang army, appointed Wenqi military commissioner, and added acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 既而溫琪臨民失政，嘗掠人之妻，為其夫所訴，罷，入為金吾大將軍。
units.en: Before long Wenqi misgoverned the people; he once seized another man's wife and was denounced by her husband. He was dismissed and appointed metropolitan guards grand general.
units.literal: Before long Wenqi in governing the people failed in administration; he once seized another man's wife and was denounced by her husband; dismissed and entered service as metropolitan guards grand general.

units.zh: 時梁末帝方姑息諸侯，重難其命，故責詞云：「若便行峻典，謂予不念功勛；
units.en: At that time Emperor Modi of Liang was indulging the feudal lords and found it difficult to issue a harsh order, so his reprimand read: "If I immediately apply severe punishment, you will say I do not remember your merit;
units.literal: At that time Liang Emperor Modi was indulging the feudal lords and found it hard to be severe in his orders, so his reprimand read: "If I immediately apply harsh law, you will say I do not remember merit;

units.zh: 若全廢舊章，謂我不安黎庶。
units.en: if I wholly set aside established law, you will say I do not care for the common people.
units.literal: if I entirely abandon old statutes, you will say I do not secure the common people.

units.zh: 為人君者，不亦難乎！」
units.en: For one who is ruler of men, is it not difficult!"
units.literal: For one who is lord of men, is it not difficult!"

units.zh: 溫琪大有愧色。
units.en: Wenqi was deeply ashamed.
units.literal: Wenqi showed great shame.

units.zh: 俄轉右監門衛上將軍、右龍武統軍。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to General of the Right Gate Guards and commander of the Right Valiant Dragons.
units.literal: Soon transferred to General of the Right Gate Guards and commander of the Right Valiant Dragons.

units.zh: 會河中朱友謙叛，權授溫琪汝州防禦使、河中行營排陣使，尋為耀州觀察留後。
units.en: When Zhu Youqian of Hezhong rebelled, Wenqi was provisionally made defense commissioner of Ruzhou and array marshal of the Hezhong campaign; soon afterward he became acting governor of Yaozhou.
units.literal: When Hezhong's Zhu Youqian rebelled, Wenqi was provisionally made Ruzhou defense commissioner and Hezhong campaign array marshal; soon after made acting governor of Yaozhou.

units.zh: 莊宗入洛，溫琪來覲，詔改耀州為順義軍，復以溫琪鎮之，加推忠向義功臣。
units.en: When Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Wenqi came to audience; an edict changed Yaozhou to the Shunyi army and again placed Wenqi in command, adding the title Merit-for-Loyalty-in-Faith.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Wenqi came to audience; an edict changed Yaozhou to the Shunyi army and again had Wenqi garrison it, adding the title Merit-for-Loyalty-in-Faith.

units.zh: 同光末，西蜀既平，命溫琪為秦州節度使。
units.en: At the end of the Tongguang era, with western Shu already pacified, Wenqi was appointed military commissioner of Qinzhou.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang, with western Shu already pacified, Wenqi was appointed Qinzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 明宗即位，因入朝，願留闕，明宗嘉而許之，除左驍衛上將軍，逐月別賜錢粟，以豐其家。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Wenqi came to court and asked to remain at the capital; Mingzong approved and appointed him General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, granting him cash and grain each month to enrich his household.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Wenqi came to court on entry and wished to remain at the capital; Mingzong praised this and granted it, appointing him General of the Left Valiant Cavalry; each month he separately received cash and grain to enrich his household.

units.zh: 逾歲，明宗謂樞密使安重誨曰：「溫琪舊人，宜選一重鎮處之。」
units.en: After a year Mingzong said to Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "Wenqi is an old acquaintance; he ought to be given an important post."
units.literal: After a year Mingzong said to Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "Wenqi is an old acquaintance; a weighty command should be chosen for him."

units.zh: 重誨奏以天下無闕。
units.en: Chonghui memorialized that there were no vacancies anywhere in the realm.
units.literal: Chonghui memorialized that there were no vacancies under heaven.

units.zh: 他日又言之，重誨素強愎，對曰：「臣累奏未有闕處，可替者，唯樞密院使而已。」
units.en: On another day he raised the matter again; Chonghui, who was by nature domineering and obstinate, replied: "Your servant has repeatedly reported that there is no vacancy; the only post that could be replaced is that of Military Affairs Commissioner itself."
units.literal: On another day he spoke of it again; Chonghui was by nature domineering and obstinate and replied: "Your servant has repeatedly memorialized that there is no vacancy; the only post that could be replaced is Military Affairs Commissioner itself."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「可。」
units.en: Mingzong said: "Very well."
units.literal: Mingzong said: "That will do."

units.zh: 重誨不能答。
units.en: Chonghui had no answer.
units.literal: Chonghui could not reply.

units.zh: 溫琪聞其事，懼為權臣所怒，幾致成疾，由是數月不出。
units.en: Wenqi heard of the exchange, feared provoking the powerful minister, nearly fell ill, and for several months did not go out.
units.literal: Wenqi heard of this affair, feared angering the powerful minister, nearly fell ill, and for this reason did not go out for several months.

units.zh: 俄拜華州節度使，依前光祿大夫、檢校太傅，進封平原郡開國公，累加食邑至三千戶。
units.en: Soon he was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou, retaining his titles as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Grand Mentor; he was advanced to Duke of Pingyuan commandery with a state fief, and his fief households were cumulatively increased to three thousand.
units.literal: Soon appointed Huazhou military commissioner, continuing as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Grand Mentor, advanced to Duke of Pingyuan commandery with state fief, and cumulatively increased fief households to three thousand.

units.zh: 溫琪至任，以己俸補葺祠廟廨舍千餘間，復於郵亭創待客之具，華而且固，往來稱之。
units.en: When Wenqi took up his post, he used his own salary to repair more than a thousand shrines and government buildings, and also furnished post stations with splendid, sturdy guest accommodations; travelers praised them.
units.literal: When Wenqi reached his post, from his own salary he repaired more than a thousand shrine and office buildings, and also at post stations created guest-reception furnishings, splendid and solid; travelers praised them.

units.zh: 清泰中，上表乞骸骨歸宋城，制以太子少保致仕。
units.en: During the Qingtai era he memorialized asking to retire to Songcheng; by decree he was granted retirement as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he memorialized asking to return his bones to Songcheng; by decree he retired as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 天福元年十二月，終於家，年七十五。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he died at home at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he died at home, aged seventy-five.

units.zh: 詔贈太子太保。
units.en: An edict posthumously awarded him Grand Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Grand Guardian to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 安崇阮，字晉臣，潞州上黨人也。
units.en: An Chongruan, courtesy name Jinchen, was a native of Shangdang in Luzhou.
units.literal: An Chongruan, style name Jinchen, was a man of Shangdang in Luzhou.

units.zh: 少倜儻，有詞辯，善騎射。
units.en: In youth he was bold and unconventional, skilled in debate, and adept at mounted archery.
units.literal: In youth he was free-spirited, had rhetorical skill, and was skilled at mounted archery.

units.zh: 父文祐，為牙門將。
units.en: His father Wenyou served as a yamen gate general.
units.literal: His father Wenyou was a yamen gate general.

units.zh: 唐光啟中，潞州軍校劉廣逐節度使高潯，據其城，僖宗詔文祐平之，既殺劉廣，召赴行在，授邛州刺史。
units.en: In the Tang Guangqi era the Luzhou army commander Liu Guang expelled the military commissioner Gao Xun and seized the city; Emperor Xizong ordered Wenyou to pacify the disturbance. After killing Liu Guang he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou.
units.literal: In the Tang Guangqi era, Luzhou army commander Liu Guang expelled military commissioner Gao Xun and seized the city; Emperor Xizong ordered Wenyou to pacify it; after killing Liu Guang he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Qiongzhou prefect.

units.zh: 其後孟方立據邢、洺，率兵攻上黨，朝廷以文祐本潞人也，授昭義節度使，令討方立，自蜀至澤州與方立戰，敗歿於陣。
units.en: Thereafter Meng Fangli held Xing and Ming and led troops against Shangdang; because Wenyou was a native of Luzhou, the court appointed him Zhaoyi military commissioner and ordered him to attack Fangli. He marched from Shu to Zezhou, fought Fangli, was defeated, and died in battle.
units.literal: Thereafter Meng Fangli held Xing and Ming, led troops to attack Shangdang; the court, because Wenyou was originally a Luzhou man, appointed him Zhaoyi military commissioner and ordered him to attack Fangli; from Shu he reached Zezhou and fought Fangli, was defeated and died on the field.

units.zh: 昭宗朝，宰臣崔魏公以文祐歿於王事，薦崇阮於朝，自是累任諸衛將軍。
units.en: During Emperor Zhaozong's reign the chief minister, the Duke of Wei, Cui, because Wenyou had died in the king's service, recommended Chongruan to court; thereafter he served repeatedly as a general of the guards.
units.literal: In Emperor Zhaozong's reign, chief minister the Duke of Wei, Cui, because Wenyou died in the king's service, recommended Chongruan to court; from this he served repeatedly as general of the guards.

units.zh: 梁氏革命，以崇阮明辯，遣使吳越，回以所獲橐裝，悉充貢奉，梁祖嘉之，故每歲乘軺於江、浙間，及回貢獻皆如初。
units.en: When the Liang house took power, because Chongruan was eloquent he was sent as envoy to Wu and Yue; on his return the goods he obtained were all submitted as tribute. The Liang founder was pleased, and each year he traveled by light carriage between the Jiang and Zhe regions; his tribute on return was always as generous as before.
units.literal: When the Liang house undertook the revolution, because Chongruan was eloquent, he was sent as envoy to Wu and Yue; on return the goods he obtained were all submitted as tribute; the Liang founder praised this, so each year he rode the light carriage between Jiang and Zhe, and on return his tribute was always as at first.

units.zh: 梁末帝嗣位，授客省使，知齊州事。
units.en: When Emperor Modi of Liang succeeded, he was appointed guest-reception commissioner and placed in charge of Qizhou affairs.
units.literal: When Liang Emperor Modi succeeded, he was appointed guest-reception commissioner and put in charge of Qizhou affairs.

units.zh: 時梁軍與莊宗對壘於河上，冀王友謙以河中叛，末帝使段凝領軍經略蒲、晉，詔崇阮監軍，又知華、雍軍府事。
units.en: At that time Liang armies faced Zhuangzong in stalemate on the Yellow River; the Prince of Ji, Youqian, rebelled at Hezhong; Emperor Modi had Duan Ning lead troops to manage Pu and Jin; an edict made Chongruan army supervisor, and he also oversaw the military prefectures of Hua and Yong.
units.literal: At that time Liang armies faced Zhuangzong in stalemate on the Yellow River; Prince of Ji Youqian rebelled at Hezhong; Emperor Modi had Duan Ning lead the army to manage Pu and Jin; an edict made Chongruan army supervisor, and he also managed Hua and Yong military prefecture affairs.

units.zh: 期年，授青州兵馬留後，入為諸衛上將軍。
units.en: After a year he was appointed acting Qingzhou horse-army commissioner and entered service as a general of the guards.
units.literal: After a year he was appointed Qingzhou horse-army acting commissioner and entered service as general of the guards.

units.zh: 唐天成中，授黔南節度使、檢校太保，尋移鎮夔州。
units.en: During the Tang Tiancheng era he was appointed military commissioner of Qiannan and acting Grand Guardian; soon afterward he was transferred to garrison Kuizhou.
units.literal: In the Tang Tiancheng era he was appointed Qiannan military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian; soon transferred to garrison Kuizhou.

units.zh: 以蜀寇侵逼，棄城歸闕，改晉州節度使，復為諸衛上將軍。
units.en: When Shu raiders pressed the borders he abandoned the city and returned to court, was reassigned as military commissioner of Jinzhou, and again became a general of the guards.
units.literal: Because Shu bandits pressed the borders, he abandoned the city and returned to court, was changed to Jinzhou military commissioner, and again became general of the guards.

units.zh: 高祖登極之二年，詔葬梁末帝，以崇阮梁之舊臣，令主葬事。
units.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign an edict ordered the burial of Emperor Modi of Liang; because Chongruan was an old minister of Liang, he was charged with overseeing the funeral.
units.literal: In the second year of Gaozu's accession, an edict buried Liang Emperor Modi; because Chongruan was an old minister of Liang, he was ordered to preside over the burial.

units.zh: 崇阮盡哀致禮，以襄其事，時人義之。
units.en: Chongruan performed the rites with full mourning and assisted the undertaking; people of the time praised his righteousness.
units.literal: Chongruan exhausted grief and performed rites to assist the affair; people of the time praised his righteousness.

units.zh: 五年，以老病請告，授右衛上將軍致仕。
units.en: In the fifth year, citing old age and illness, he requested leave and was granted retirement as General of the Right Guards.
units.literal: In the fifth year, on account of old age and illness he requested leave and was granted retirement as General of the Right Guards.

units.zh: 開運元年九月，卒於西京。
units.en: In the ninth month of the first year of Kaiyun he died at the western capital.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Kaiyun he died at the western capital.

units.zh: 贈太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand Mentor.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 楊彥詢，字成章，河中寶鼎人。
units.en: Yang Yanxun, courtesy name Chengzhang, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
units.literal: Yang Yanxun, style name Chengzhang, was a man of Baoding in Hezhong.

units.zh: 父規，累贈少師。
units.en: His father Gui was repeatedly posthumously awarded the title Junior Mentor.
units.literal: His father Gui was repeatedly posthumously awarded Junior Mentor.

units.zh: 彥詢年十三，事青帥王師範，有書萬卷，以彥詢聰悟，使掌之。
units.en: At thirteen Yanxun entered the service of the Qing prefect Wang Shifan, who possessed ten thousand volumes of books; because Yanxun was quick-witted, Shifan put him in charge of them.
units.literal: At age thirteen Yanxun served Qing prefect Wang Shifan, who had ten thousand volumes of books; because Yanxun was clever, he was put in charge of them.

units.zh: 及長，益加親信，常委監護郡兵。
units.en: As he grew older he won still greater trust and was regularly entrusted to supervise the prefectural troops.
units.literal: When he grew up, trust increased further and he was regularly entrusted to supervise the prefectural troops.

units.zh: 及梁將楊師厚降下青州，彥詢隨師範歸命。
units.en: When the Liang general Yang Shihou took Qingzhou, Yanxun followed Shifan in submitting.
units.literal: When Liang general Yang Shihou reduced Qingzhou, Yanxun followed Shifan in submitting.

units.zh: 洎師範見殺，楊師厚領鄴，召置麾下，俾掌賓客。
units.en: By the time Shifan was killed, Yang Shihou held Ye and summoned Yanxun to his staff, putting him in charge of guests.
units.literal: By the time Shifan was killed, Yang Shihou took Ye and summoned Yanxun under his banner, putting him in charge of guests.

units.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，復事焉。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, he again entered his service.
units.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, he again served him.

units.zh: 同光元年冬，從平大梁，升為引進副使，將命西川及淮南稱旨，累遷內職。
units.en: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the pacification of Daliang, was promoted to deputy introducing commissioner, carried out missions to western Shu and Huainan to the emperor's satisfaction, and rose repeatedly in inner-court posts.
units.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed in pacifying Daliang, was promoted to deputy introducing commissioner, carried missions to western Shu and Huainan to the emperor's satisfaction, and was repeatedly promoted in inner-court posts.

units.zh: 明宗時，為客省使、檢校司徒，使兩浙回，授德州刺史。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served as guest-reception commissioner and acting Minister of Works; after a mission to the two Zhes he was appointed prefect of Dezhou.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time he was guest-reception commissioner and acting Minister of Works; after a mission to the two Zhes he was appointed Dezhou prefect.

units.zh: 末帝即位，改羽林將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Modi took the throne, he was made general of the Forest of Feathers.
units.literal: When Emperor Modi took the throne, he was changed to Forest of Feathers general.

units.zh: 時高祖鎮太原，朝廷疑貳，以彥詢沈厚，擇充北京副留守。
units.en: At that time Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan; the court was suspicious of his loyalty and, because Yanxun was steady and thoughtful, chose him as deputy garrison commander of the northern capital.
units.literal: At that time Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan; the court suspected disloyalty and, because Yanxun was deep and steady, chose him as deputy garrison commander of the northern capital.

units.zh: 清泰末，以宋審虔為北京留守，高祖深懷不足，以情告彥詢。
units.en: At the end of the Qingtai era Song Shenqian was made garrison commander of the northern capital; Gaozu was deeply displeased and confided his feelings to Yanxun.
units.literal: At the end of Qingtai, Song Shenqian was made northern capital garrison commander; Gaozu was deeply displeased and confided his feelings to Yanxun.

units.zh: 彥詢恐高祖失臣節，乃曰：「不知太原兵甲芻粟幾何，可敵大國否？
units.en: Yanxun feared that Gaozu would abandon his duty as a subject and said: "I do not know how much armor, fodder, and grain Taiyuan possesses—can it stand against the great state or not?
units.literal: Yanxun feared Gaozu would lose the minister's proper stance and said: "I do not know how much military armor, fodder, and grain Taiyuan has—can it match the great state or not?

units.zh: 請明公反覆慮之。」
units.en: I beg the Illustrious Lord to weigh the matter again and again."
units.literal: I beg the Illustrious Lord to consider this back and forth."

units.zh: 蓋欲回其意也。
units.en: He meant thereby to turn Gaozu's mind.
units.literal: He intended thereby to turn back Gaozu's resolve.

units.zh: 高祖曰：「我不忿小人相代，方寸決矣。」
units.en: Gaozu said: "I cannot endure being displaced by petty men; my mind is made up."
units.literal: Gaozu said: "I cannot bear that petty men should replace me; my mind is made up."

units.zh: 彥詢知其不可諫，遂止。
units.en: Yanxun knew he could not be dissuaded and said no more.
units.literal: Yanxun knew he could not be dissuaded and stopped.

units.zh: 左右欲害之，高祖曰：「唯副使一人我自保，明爾勿復言也。」
units.en: Those around Gaozu wished to harm him; Gaozu said: "I alone will protect the deputy commissioner—understand this and say no more of it."
units.literal: Those around Gaozu wished to harm him; Gaozu said: "I alone will protect the deputy commissioner—understand this and speak no more of it."

units.zh: 及即位，授齊州防禦使、檢校太保，旋改宣徽使。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, he appointed Yanxun defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian, then soon made him palace treasury commissioner.
units.literal: When he took the throne, he appointed Yanxun defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian; soon after he was changed to palace treasury commissioner.

units.zh: 從高祖入洛，加左驍衛上將軍兼職。
units.en: He followed Gaozu into Luoyang and was additionally appointed Left Valiant Cavalry supreme general.
units.literal: He followed Gaozu into Luoyang and was given the additional post of Left Valiant Cavalry supreme general.

units.zh: 天福二年秋，出為鄧州節度使，歲餘，入為宣徽使。
units.en: In autumn of Tianfu 2 he was sent out as military commissioner of Dengzhou; after more than a year he returned to court as palace treasury commissioner.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Tianfu he went out as military commissioner of Dengzhou; after more than a year he entered court as palace treasury commissioner.

units.zh: 四年，使於契丹。
units.en: In the fourth year he was dispatched on embassy to the Khitan.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was sent on mission to the Khitan.

units.zh: 六年春，授邢州節度使、檢校太傅。
units.en: In spring of the sixth year he was made military commissioner of Xingzhou and acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: In spring of the sixth year he was appointed military commissioner of Xingzhou and acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 時鎮州安重榮有不臣之狀，彥詢憂其窺伺，會車駕幸鄴，表求入覲。
units.en: At that time An Chongrong of Zhenzhou showed signs of rebellion, and Yanxun feared he was watching for an opportunity. When the emperor visited Ye, Yanxun memorialized requesting an audience.
units.literal: At that time An Chongrong of Zhenzhou showed signs of disloyalty; Yanxun feared he would watch for an opening. It happened that the imperial carriage visited Ye; Yanxun submitted a memorial requesting an audience.

units.zh: 高祖慮契丹怒安重榮之殺行人也，移兵犯境，復命彥詢使焉，仍恐重榮要之，由滄州路以入蕃。
units.en: Gaozu feared the Khitan would be angered that An Chongrong had killed envoys and would march against the border. He again sent Yanxun on embassy, still fearing Chongrong might intercept him, and had him enter Khitan territory by way of Cangzhou.
units.literal: Gaozu feared the Khitan would be angered that An Chongrong had killed envoys and would move troops to violate the border; he again ordered Yanxun on embassy, still fearing Chongrong might intercept him, so he entered the barbarian lands by the Cangzhou route.

units.zh: 戎主果怒重榮，彥詢具言非高祖本意，蓋如人家惡子，無如之何。
units.en: The Khitan ruler was indeed angry at Chongrong. Yanxun explained at length that this was not Gaozu's intent—it was like a wicked son in one's household, whom one cannot control.
units.literal: The barbarian lord was indeed angry at Chongrong; Yanxun fully explained it was not Gaozu's original intent—it was like a family's wicked son, whom one cannot help.

units.zh: 尋聞重榮犯闕，乃放還。
units.en: When he soon heard that Chongrong had marched on the capital, they sent Yanxun back.
units.literal: Soon after hearing Chongrong had invaded the capital precincts, they released Yanxun to return.

units.zh: 七年春，授華州節度使、檢校太尉。
units.en: In spring of the seventh year he was made military commissioner of Huazhou and acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In spring of the seventh year he was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou and acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 在任二年，屬部內蝗旱，道堇相望，彥詢以官粟假貸，州民賴之存濟者甚眾。
units.en: During his two years in office the prefecture suffered locusts and drought, and corpses lined the roads. Yanxun lent out official grain, and very many of the people survived by it.
units.literal: During two years in office, locusts and drought afflicted the prefecture; corpses lay along the roads. Yanxun lent out official grain; very many of the prefectural people relied on this for survival.

units.zh: 開運初，以風痹授右金吾衛上將軍，俄卒於官，年七十四。
