units.en: At the beginning of Kaiyun he suffered a paralytic stroke and was made Left Golden Valiants supreme general; he soon died in office at seventy-four.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was given wind paralysis and appointed Left Golden Valiants supreme general; soon he died in office at age seventy-four.

units.zh: 贈太子太師。
units.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 李承約，字德儉，薊州人也。
units.en: Li Chengyue, courtesy name Dejian, was a native of Jizhou.
units.literal: Li Chengyue, style name Dejian, was a man of Jizhou.

units.zh: 曾祖瓊，薊州別駕，贈工部尚書。
units.en: His great-grandfather Qiong served as vice prefect of Jizhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Qiong was Jizhou vice prefect, posthumously awarded Minister of Works.

units.zh: 祖安仁，檀州刺史，贈太子太保。
units.en: His grandfather Anren was prefect of Tanzhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as Crown Prince Grand Guardian.
units.literal: His grandfather Anren was Tanzhou prefect, posthumously awarded Crown Prince Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 父君操，平州刺史，贈太子少師。
units.en: His father Juncao was prefect of Pingzhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as Crown Prince Junior Tutor.
units.literal: His father Juncao was Pingzhou prefect, posthumously awarded Crown Prince Junior Tutor.

units.zh: 承約性剛健篤實，少習武事，弱冠為幽州牙門校，遷山後八軍巡檢使。
units.en: Chengyue was by nature sturdy, steadfast, and sincere. In youth he trained in military affairs. At twenty he was a company commander of the Ya Gate guard at Youzhou, then was promoted to inspector of the eight armies behind the mountains.
units.literal: Chengyue's nature was firm, healthy, and sincere; in youth he studied military affairs. At weak adulthood he was a Ya Gate company commander of Youzhou, then promoted to inspector of the eight armies behind the mountains.

units.zh: 屬劉守光囚殺父兄，名儒宿將經事父兄者，多無辜被戮，自以握兵在外，心不自安。
units.en: When Liu Shouguang imprisoned and killed his father and elder brothers, many renowned scholars and veteran generals who had served them were slaughtered without cause. Chengyue, holding troops abroad, could not feel secure.
units.literal: When Liu Shouguang imprisoned and killed his father and elder brothers, renowned Confucians and veteran generals who had served his father and brothers were for the most part innocently executed. Chengyue, holding troops outside, was ill at ease in his heart.

units.zh: 時屬唐武皇召募英豪，方開霸業，乃以所部二千歸於并州，即補匡霸都指揮使、檢校右僕射兼領貝州刺史。
units.en: At that time Emperor Wuzong of Tang was recruiting heroes and building his hegemony. Chengyue brought his two thousand men to Bingzhou and was at once appointed commander of the Suppressing-Bahe capital guard, acting Right Vice Minister, and concurrent prefect of Beizhou.
units.literal: At that time Tang Emperor Wuzong was recruiting heroes and opening hegemony; Chengyue brought his command of two thousand to Bingzhou. He was immediately appointed Commander of the Suppressing-Bahe Capital and acting Right Vice Minister, concurrently holding Beizhou prefect.

units.zh: 從破夾寨，及與梁人戰於臨清有功，再遷洺、汾二州。
units.en: He took part in breaking the encirclement and distinguished himself fighting Liang at Linqing, then was transferred twice to Luo and Fen.
units.literal: He followed in breaking the encirclement and had merit fighting Liang at Linqing; he was twice transferred to Luo and Fen prefectures.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，授檢校司空、磁州刺史，為治平直，移授潁州團練使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, Chengyue was appointed acting Minister of Works and prefect of Cizhou. His administration was fair and upright, and he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, Chengyue was appointed acting Minister of Works and Cizhou prefect; his governance was fair and upright, and he was transferred to be regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 天成中，以邠州節度使毛璋將圖不軌，乃命為涇州節度副使，且承密旨往偵之。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era, when Binzhou military commissioner Mao Zhang was plotting rebellion, Chengyue was ordered to serve as deputy military commissioner of Jingzhou and was also given a secret edict to investigate him.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era, because Binzhou military commissioner Mao Zhang was plotting disloyalty, Chengyue was ordered to be deputy military commissioner of Jingzhou and moreover carried a secret edict to spy on him.

units.zh: 既至，以善言諭之，璋乃受代。
units.en: When he arrived, he won Zhang over with persuasive words, and Zhang then agreed to be replaced.
units.literal: When he arrived, he persuaded Zhang with fine words; Zhang then accepted replacement.

units.zh: 明宗賞其能，加檢校太保，拜黔南節度使。
units.en: Emperor Mingzong rewarded his ability with acting Grand Guardian and appointed him military commissioner of Qiannan.
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong rewarded his ability, added acting Grand Guardian, and appointed him military commissioner of Qiannan.

units.zh: 數年之間，巴、邛蠻蜑不敢犯境，外勸農桑，內興學校，兇邪盡去，民皆感之，故父老數輩重趼詣闕，言其政化。
units.en: Within a few years the Ba, Qiong tribes, and Dan raiders no longer dared cross the border. He promoted farming and sericulture abroad and founded schools at home; the wicked were driven out, and the people were deeply grateful. Several elders therefore traveled to the capital with feet calloused from the long journey to praise his governance.
units.literal: Within several years the Ba, Qiong barbarians and Dan raiders did not dare violate the border; externally he encouraged farming and sericulture, internally he raised schools—the vicious and evil were wholly removed, and the people were all moved. Hence several elders, their feet heavily calloused, went to the capital to speak of his civilizing rule.

units.zh: 又聽留周歲，征為左衛上將軍，自左龍武統軍加特進、檢校太傅，充昭義軍節度使，賜推忠奉節翊戴功臣。
units.en: He was permitted to remain another year, then recalled as Left Guard supreme general. From commander of the Left Valiant Dragons he received extraordinary promotion and acting Grand Tutor, was made military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, and granted the title Loyal, Observant, and Throne-Supporting Subject.
units.literal: He was again allowed to remain one full year, then summoned as Left Guard supreme general; from Left Valiant Dragon commander-in-chief he received extraordinary promotion and acting Grand Tutor, was made military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, and granted the honorific subject who supports loyalty, observes propriety, and assists the throne.

units.zh: 歲餘歸朝，復為左龍武統軍。
units.en: After more than a year he returned to court and again became commander of the Left Valiant Dragons.
units.literal: After more than a year he returned to court and again served as Left Valiant Dragon commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 高祖禦宇之二年，授左驍衛上將軍，進封開國公，累上表請老，尋以病卒，時年七十五。
units.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign he was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry supreme general and enfeoffed as Duke Who Opens the State. He repeatedly memorialized asking to retire, but soon died of illness at seventy-five.
units.literal: In the second year of Gaozu's reign he was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry supreme general and advanced to Duke Who Opens the State; he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement; soon he died of illness at age seventy-five.

units.zh: 贈太子太師。
units.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 陸思鐸，澶州臨黃人。
units.en: Lu Siduo was a native of Linhuang in Chanzhou.
units.literal: Lu Siduo was a man of Linhuang in Chanzhou.

units.zh: 父再端，贈光祿卿。
units.en: His father Zaiduan was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: His father Zaiduan was posthumously awarded Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 思鐸有武幹，梁太祖領四鎮，隸於麾下。
units.en: Siduo had martial talent. When the Liang founding emperor held the four commands, Siduo served under his banner.
units.literal: Siduo had martial ability; when Liang founding emperor held the four commands he served under his banner.

units.zh: 及即位，授廣武都指揮使，歷突陣、拱辰軍使，積前後戰勛，累官至檢校司徒、拱辰左廂都指揮使，遙領恩州刺史。
units.en: When the emperor took the throne, Siduo was appointed commander of the Expansive Martial army and served as commander of the Sudden Array and Bowing to Heaven armies. With repeated battle honors he rose to acting Minister of Works, commander of the left wing of the Bowing to Heaven army, and titular prefect of Enzhou.
units.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Siduo was appointed commander of the Expansive Martial army; he served as commanders of the Sudden Array and Bowing to Heaven armies. With accumulated battle merit before and after, he rose to acting Minister of Works, commander of the left wing of the Bowing to Heaven army, and held Enzhou prefect in title only.

units.zh: 初，梁軍與莊宗對壘於河上，思鐸以善射，日預其戰。
units.en: Earlier, when Liang and Zhuangzong faced each other across the Yellow River, Siduo, skilled in archery, fought in the battles every day.
units.literal: Early on, when Liang and Zhuangzong faced each other across the river, Siduo was skilled in archery and daily took part in the fighting.

units.zh: 嘗於箭笴之上自鏤其姓名，一日射中莊宗之馬鞍，莊宗拔箭視之，睹思鐸姓名，因而記之。
units.en: He once carved his name into an arrow shaft. One day he shot and struck Emperor Zhuangzong's saddle. Zhuangzong drew out the arrow, saw Siduo's name carved on it, and remembered him.
units.literal: Once he carved his own name on an arrow shaft; one day he shot and struck Emperor Zhuangzong's saddle; Zhuangzong drew out the arrow and looked at it, saw Siduo's name, and thereby remembered him.

units.zh: 及莊宗平梁，思鐸以例來降，莊宗出箭以視之，思鐸伏地待罪，莊宗慰而釋之。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Siduo surrendered according to precedent. Zhuangzong produced the arrow to show him. Siduo prostrated himself to await punishment, but Zhuangzong comforted him and let him go.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Siduo came to surrender per precedent; Zhuangzong produced the arrow to show him. Siduo prostrated himself awaiting punishment; Zhuangzong comforted and released him.

units.zh: 尋授龍武右廂都指揮使，加檢校太保。
units.en: Soon he was made commander of the right wing of the Valiant Dragon army and acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed commander of the right wing of the Valiant Dragon army and given acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 天成中，為深州刺史，改雄捷右廂馬軍都指揮使。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was prefect of Shenzhou, then became commander of the right-wing cavalry of the Valiant Achievers.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was Shenzhou prefect, then changed to commander of the right-wing horse army of the Valiant Achievers.

units.zh: 會南伐荊門，思鐸亦預其行。
units.en: When the court campaigned south against Jingmen, Siduo took part as well.
units.literal: When they campaigned south against Jingmen, Siduo also took part.

units.zh: 時高季興以舟兵拒王師，思鐸每發矢中敵，則洞胸達掖，由是賊鋒稍挫，不敢輕進，諸軍鹹壯之。
units.en: At that time Gao Jixing used naval forces to resist the imperial army. Whenever Siduo's arrow found its mark, it pierced clean through from chest to armpit. The enemy vanguard was thus checked and no longer dared press forward rashly, and the armies took heart.
units.literal: At that time Gao Jixing used boat troops to resist the imperial army; whenever Siduo loosed an arrow that hit the enemy, it pierced through chest to armpit. Thereby the rebels' spearhead was somewhat checked and they did not dare advance lightly; all the armies were heartened.

units.zh: 高祖革命，拜陳州刺史，秩滿，歷左神武、羽林二統軍，出為蔡州刺史，遇代歸朝。
units.en: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, Siduo was appointed prefect of Chenzhou. After his term ended he served in succession as commander of the Left Divine Martial and Forest of Plumes armies, was sent out as prefect of Caizhou, and returned to court when replaced.
units.literal: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, Siduo was made Chenzhou prefect. When his term expired he served in succession as commander of the Left Divine Martial and Forest of Plumes armies, went out as Caizhou prefect, and on replacement returned to court.

units.zh: 天福八年，以疾卒，時年五十四。
units.en: In Tianfu 8 he died of illness at fifty-four.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness at age fifty-four.

units.zh: 思鐸典陳郡日，甚有惠政，常戒諸子曰：「我死則藏骨於宛丘，使我棲魂於所治之地。」
units.en: While governing Chen commandery Siduo carried out benevolent policies and often warned his sons, saying, "When I die, bury my bones at Wansui and let my soul rest in the land I governed."
units.literal: While Siduo governed Chen commandery he had very benevolent policies and often admonished his sons, saying: "When I die, bury my bones at Wansui; let my soul dwell in the land I governed."

units.zh: 及卒，乃葬於陳，從其志也。
units.en: When he died they buried him at Chen, as he had wished.
units.literal: When he died, they buried him at Chen, following his wish.

units.zh: 安元信，朔州馬邑人也。
units.en: An Yuanxin was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
units.literal: An Yuanxin was a man of Mayi in Shuozhou.

units.zh: 少善騎射。
units.en: In youth he excelled at mounted archery.
units.literal: In youth he was skilled in mounted archery.

units.zh: 後唐莊宗為晉王時，元信詣軍門求自效。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang was still Prince of Jin, Yuanxin came to the army gate to offer his service.
units.literal: When Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin, Yuanxin came to the army gate to offer his service.

units.zh: 尋隸明宗麾下，累從明宗征討有功，明宗即位，擢為捧聖軍使，加檢校兵部尚書。
units.en: He soon entered Mingzong's service and followed him on repeated campaigns with distinction. When Mingzong took the throne he was promoted to commander of the Upholding Sagacity army and acting Minister of War.
units.literal: Soon he served under Mingzong's banner, followed Mingzong repeatedly in campaigns with merit. When Mingzong took the throne he was promoted to commander of the Upholding Sagacity army and given acting Minister of War.

units.zh: 清泰三年，遷雄義都指揮使，受詔屯於代州，太守張朗遇之甚厚，元信亦以兄事之。
units.en: In Qingtai 3 he was transferred to commander of the Valiant Righteous army and ordered to garrison at Daizhou. The defender Zhang Lang treated him very generously, and Yuanxin in turn treated him as an elder brother.
units.literal: In the third year of Qingtai he was transferred to commander of the Valiant Righteous army and ordered to garrison at Daizhou. Defender Zhang Lang treated him very generously; Yuanxin also treated him as an elder brother.

units.zh: 是歲五月，高祖建義於太原，俄聞契丹有約赴難，元信入說朗曰：「張敬達雖圍太原，而兵尚未合，代郡當雁門之沖，敵至其何以禦？
units.en: That year in the fifth month Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan. Soon word came that the Khitan had agreed to come to his aid. Yuanxin went to persuade Lang, saying, "Zhang Jingda may have besieged Taiyuan, but his forces are not yet fully gathered. Dai commandery stands at the throat of Wild Goose Gate—when the enemy arrives, how will you defend it?
units.literal: That year in the fifth month Gaozu raised righteousness at Taiyuan; soon they heard the Khitan had agreed to come to the rescue. Yuanxin went in to persuade Lang, saying: "Though Zhang Jingda has besieged Taiyuan, the armies are not yet united; Daic commandery stands at the throat of Wild Goose Gate—when the enemy arrives, how will it be defended?

units.zh: 仆觀石令公素長者，舉必成事，若使人道意歸款，俟其兩端，亦求全之上策也。」
units.en: I see that Lord Shi has always been a man of stature, and his cause is sure to prevail. If you send someone to convey your intent to submit and keep your options open, that is the best way to preserve yourself."
units.literal: I observe that Lord Shi has always been a man of stature; his undertaking will surely succeed. If one sends someone to convey intent to submit and tender allegiance, waiting until he stands between two sides—that too is the superior policy of preserving oneself whole."

units.zh: 朗不納，元信悔以誠言之，反相猜忌。
units.en: Lang would not listen. Yuanxin regretted having spoken frankly, and thereafter they grew suspicious of each other.
units.literal: Lang would not accept it; Yuanxin regretted speaking sincerely, and instead they were mutually suspicious.

units.zh: 尋聞安重榮、安審信相次以騎兵赴太原，元信遂率部曲以歸高祖。
units.en: When he soon heard that An Chongrong and An Shenxin had in succession led cavalry to Taiyuan, Yuanxin led his personal troops to join Gaozu.
units.literal: Soon they heard An Chongrong and An Shenxin in succession led cavalry to Taiyuan; Yuanxin then led his personal troops to join Gaozu.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：元信謀殺朗，不克，帥其眾奔審信，審信遂帥麾下數百騎，與元信掠百井奔晉陽。）〉
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Yuanxin plotted to kill Lang but failed, then led his men to join Shenxin. Shenxin then led several hundred horsemen under his command, together with Yuanxin, to raid Baijing and flee to Jinyang.)〉
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Yuanxin plotted to kill Lang but failed; he led his troops to join Shenxin, and Shenxin then led the several hundred horsemen under his command together with Yuanxin to plunder Baijing and flee to Jinyang.)〉

units.zh: 高祖見之喜，謂元信曰：「爾睹何利害，背強歸弱？」
units.en: Gaozu was delighted to see him and said to Yuanxin, "What did you see in the balance of advantage and harm, that you abandoned the strong to join the weak?"
units.literal: Gaozu was pleased to see him and said to Yuanxin, "What advantage and harm did you see, that you turned your back on the strong to join the weak?"

units.zh: 元信曰：「某非知星識氣，唯以人事斷之。
units.en: Yuanxin said, "I do not read the stars or discern the qi of the age—I judge only by human affairs.
units.literal: Yuanxin said: "I do not know stars or discern qi—I judge only by human affairs.

units.zh: 夫帝王者，出語行令，示人以信。
units.en: A man who would be emperor speaks and acts in a way that shows the people he can be trusted.
units.literal: The man who would be emperor issues words, carries out orders, and shows the people trustworthiness.

units.zh: 嘗聞主上許令公河東一生，今遽改之，是自欺也。
units.en: I once heard that the present sovereign promised Lord Shi Hedong for life, yet now he suddenly revokes it—that is deceiving himself.
units.literal: I once heard that the present sovereign promised Lord Shi a lifetime in Hedong; now he suddenly changes it—that is deceiving himself.

units.zh: 且令公國之密親，親尚不能保，肯保天下之心乎！
units.en: Moreover Lord Shi is the state's close kin. If he cannot even protect his own kin, how can he win the hearts of the realm!
units.literal: Moreover Lord Shi is the state's close kin; if kin cannot even be preserved, how could he preserve the heart of All-under-Heaven!

units.zh: 以斯而言，見其亡也，何得為強也。」
units.en: From that one sees his ruin—how can he be called strong?"
units.literal: By that reasoning one sees his ruin—how could he be called strong?"

units.zh: 高祖知其誠，因開懷納之，委以戎事。
units.en: Gaozu knew he spoke sincerely, welcomed him wholeheartedly, and entrusted him with military affairs.
units.literal: Gaozu knew his sincerity, therefore opened his heart and accepted him, entrusting military affairs to him.

units.zh: 高祖即位之元年，授耀州團練使，加檢校太保。
units.en: In the first year of Gaozu's reign he was appointed regimental commissioner of Yaozhou and acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: In the first year of Gaozu's reign he was appointed regimental commissioner of Yaozhou and given acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 四年，入為右神武統軍，其年八月，復出牧洺州。
units.en: In the fourth year he entered court as commander of the Right Divine Martial army; that same year, in the eighth month, he was again sent out to govern Luozhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Right Divine Martial commander-in-chief; that year in the eighth month he again went out to govern Luozhou.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，尋遷宿州，九年，罷任來朝。
units.en: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, he was soon transferred to Suzhou. In the ninth year his term ended and he returned to court.
units.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, he was soon transferred to Suzhou; in the ninth year his appointment ended and he came to court.

units.zh: 開運初，授復州防禦使。
units.en: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was appointed defense commissioner of Fuzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was appointed defense commissioner of Fuzhou.

units.zh: 三年，卒於任，年六十三。
units.en: In the third year he died in office at sixty-three.
units.literal: In the third year he died in office at age sixty-three.

units.zh: 贈太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 張朗，徐州蕭縣人。
units.en: Zhang Lang was a native of Xiaoxian in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Lang was a man of Xiaoxian in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 父楚，贈工部尚書。
units.en: His father Chu was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
units.literal: His father Chu was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.

units.zh: 朗年十八，善射，膂力過人，鄉里敬憚之，梁祖聞其名，就補蕭縣鎮使，充吾縣都遊奕使，時朗年才二十三。
units.en: At eighteen Lang was skilled in archery and unusually strong; his neighbors both respected and feared him. The Liang founding ancestor heard of him and appointed him garrison commander of Xiaoxian and touring commissioner of the district—Lang was then only twenty-three.
units.literal: At eighteen Lang was skilled in archery; his strength exceeded others; his village respected and feared him. Liang founding ancestor heard his name and appointed him Xiaoxian garrison commander, filling the post of touring commissioner of our district—Lang was then only twenty-three.

units.zh: 歲餘，補宣武軍內衙都將，歷洛州步軍、曹州開武、汴州十內衙、鄆州都指揮使。
units.en: After more than a year he became an inner-palace commander of the Xuanwu army and served in succession as Luozhou infantry commander, Caozhou Kaiwu commander, one of Bianzhou's ten inner-palace commanders, and Yunzhou army commander.
units.literal: After more than a year he was appointed inner-palace commander of the Xuanwu army, and served as Luozhou infantry commander, Caozhou Kaiwu commander, Bianzhou ten inner-palace commands, and Yunzhou army commander.

units.zh: 梁末，從招討使段凝襲衛州，下之，遂授衛州刺史。
units.en: Late in Liang he followed pacification commissioner Duan Ning in attacking Weizhou, took it, and was appointed prefect of Weizhou.
units.literal: At the end of Liang he followed pacification commissioner Duan Ning in striking Weizhou, took it, and was then appointed Weizhou prefect.

units.zh: 事梁僅三年，凡有征討，無不預之。
units.en: In only three years of service to Liang he took part in every campaign.
units.literal: In serving Liang only three years, whenever there was campaigning he never failed to take part.

units.zh: 同光三年，從魏王繼岌伐蜀，為先鋒橋道使。
units.en: In Tongguang 3 he followed Prince of Wei Jiji in the Shu campaign as vanguard bridge-and-road commissioner.
units.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he followed Prince of Wei Jiji in the Shu campaign as vanguard bridge-and-road commissioner.

units.zh: 明宗朝，歷興、忠、登三州刺史。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served in succession as prefect of Xing, Zhong, and Deng.
units.literal: In the Mingzong reign he served in succession as prefect of Xing, Zhong, and Deng prefectures.

units.zh: 清泰初，以契丹犯邊，補西北面行營步軍都指揮使，從高祖屯軍於代北，俄兼代州刺史，又改行營諸軍馬步都虞候。
units.en: At the beginning of Qingtai, when the Khitan raided the border, he was appointed northwestern campaign infantry commander-in-chief, followed Gaozu in garrisoning northern Dai, soon also served concurrently as prefect of Daizhou, and was later made chief adjutant of horse and foot for the campaign armies.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, because the Khitan violated the border, he was appointed northwestern campaign infantry commander-in-chief, followed Gaozu in garrisoning the north of Dai, soon also held Daizhou prefect concurrently, and was again changed to campaign armies horse-and-foot chief adjutant.

units.zh: 高祖建義於太原，遣使以書諭之，朗曰：「為人臣而有二心可乎！」
units.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan he sent envoys with letters urging him to submit. Lang said, "Can a subject harbor two hearts!"
units.literal: When Gaozu raised righteousness at Taiyuan he sent envoys with letters to instruct him. Lang said: "Can one who serves as minister have two hearts!"

units.zh: 乃斬其使。
units.en: He then beheaded the envoys.
units.literal: He then beheaded the envoys.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：帝以晉安已降，遣使諭諸州，代州刺史張朗斬其使。
units.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Because Jin'an had already surrendered, the emperor sent envoys to instruct the various prefectures, but Zhang Lang, prefect of Daizhou, beheaded his envoys.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: The emperor, because Jin'an had already surrendered, sent envoys to instruct the various prefectures; Zhang Lang, prefect of Daizhou, beheaded his envoys.

units.zh: 蓋晉祖初起，安元信勸朗歸順，不從，至是復斬其使也。）〉
units.en: When the Jin founder first rose, An Yuanxin had urged Lang to submit, but he refused; now he again beheaded the envoys.)〉
units.literal: This was because when the Jin founder first rose, An Yuanxin urged Lang to submit but he would not; now once again he beheaded the envoys.)〉

units.zh: 洎高祖入洛，領全師朝覲，授貝州防禦使，在任數歲。
units.en: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Lang led his entire army to audience and was appointed defense commissioner of Beizhou, where he served several years.
units.literal: By the time Gaozu entered Luoyang, Lang led his entire army to audience and was appointed defense commissioner of Beizhou, serving several years in office.

units.zh: 天福五年，除左羽林統軍，六年，授光祿大夫、檢校太傅、慶州刺史。
units.en: In Tianfu 5 he was made commander of the Left Forest of Plumes; in the sixth year he was given Grandee Counsellor of State, acting Grand Tutor, and prefect of Qingzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was removed to Left Forest of Plumes commander-in-chief; in the sixth year he was given Grandee Counsellor of State, acting Grand Tutor, and Qingzhou prefect.

units.zh: 在官二年卒，年七十四。
units.en: He died in office after two years at seventy-four.
units.literal: He died in office after two years at age seventy-four.

units.zh: 李德充，應州金城人。
units.en: Li Dechong was a native of Jincheng in Yingzhou.
units.literal: Li Dechong was a man of Jincheng in Yingzhou.

units.zh: 祖晟，父宗元，皆為邊將。
units.en: His grandfather Sheng and his father Zongyuan were both frontier generals.
units.literal: His grandfather was Sheng and his father Zongyuan; both were frontier generals.

units.zh: 德充少善騎射，事後唐武皇為偏校。
units.en: In youth Dechong was skilled at horsemanship and archery and served Wuhuang of Later Tang as a junior officer.
units.literal: Dechong in youth was skilled at horsemanship and archery and served Wuhuang of Later Tang as a junior officer.

units.zh: 及從莊宗戰潞州、柏鄉、德勝渡，繼有軍功，累加檢校尚書左僕射，遙食郡俸。
units.en: Following Zhuangzong at Luzhou, Baixiang, and Desheng Ford, he repeatedly earned military merit and rose to acting Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue with commandery salary in absentia.
units.literal: When he followed Zhuangzong in battles at Luzhou, Baixiang, and Desheng Ford, he repeatedly earned military merit and was repeatedly promoted to acting Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, drawing commandery salary in absentia.

units.zh: 天成中，檢校司空，領蔚州刺史。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was made acting Minister of Works and prefect of Yu Prefecture.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was made acting Minister of Works and appointed prefect of Yu Prefecture.

units.zh: 長興元年，授雄武軍節度、秦成階觀察處置等使，加檢校司徒。
units.en: In the first year of Changxing he was made military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Qin, Cheng, Jie, and Guan, with acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: In the first year of Changxing he was appointed military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Qin, Cheng, Jie, and Guan, and given acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 二年六月，移鎮定州，充北面副招討使。
units.en: In the sixth month of the second year he was transferred to garrison Dingzhou as deputy northern suppression commissioner.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the second year he was transferred to garrison Dingzhou and served as deputy northern suppression commissioner.

units.zh: 高祖即位，改鎮涇原，及受代歸闕，會高祖幸鄴，授東京留守，加同平章事。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Dechong was transferred to command Jingyuan. After he was relieved and returned to court, Gaozu happened to be visiting Ye and appointed him regent of the Eastern Capital with concurrent grand councilor.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Dechong was transferred to command Jingyuan. When he was relieved and returned to court, Gaozu happened to be visiting Ye; he was appointed regent of the Eastern Capital and given concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，移廣晉尹，加檢校太師。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made Guangjin Intendant and acting Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was transferred to Guangjin Intendant and given acting Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 開運中，再領涇州，以病卒於鎮。
units.en: During Kaiyun he again held Jingzhou and died of illness in office.
units.literal: In the Kaiyun era he again held Jingzhou and died of illness in his command.

units.zh: 德充幼與明宗俱事武皇，故後之諸將多兄事之，時謂之「李七哥」。
units.en: Dechong had served Wuhuang together with Mingzong in youth, so later generals often treated him as an elder brother and called him "Seventh Brother Li."
units.literal: Dechong in youth served Wuhuang together with Mingzong, so later generals often treated him as an elder brother, and at the time he was called "Seventh Brother Li."

units.zh: 所治之地，雖無殊政，然以寬恕及物，家無濫積，亦武將之廉者。
units.en: In the places he governed he had no extraordinary policies, but he treated people with leniency and kept no excessive hoard at home; he was counted among the frugal military commanders.
units.literal: In the places he governed, though he had no extraordinary policies, he treated people with leniency and his household had no excessive hoardings; he was also a frugal man among military commanders.

units.zh: 田武，字德偉，大名元城人。
units.en: Tian Wu, courtesy name Dewei, was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.
units.literal: Tian Wu, style name Dewei, was a man of Yuancheng in Daming.

units.zh: 父簡，累贈右僕射。
units.en: His father Jian received repeated posthumous promotions to Right Vice Minister.
units.literal: His father Jian was repeatedly posthumously awarded Right Vice Minister.

units.zh: 武少有拳勇，初事莊宗為小校，歷遷勝節指揮使。
units.en: Wu in youth was bold in hand-to-hand fighting. He first served Zhuangzong as a petty officer and rose in succession to commander of the Shengjie army.
units.literal: Wu in youth had fist courage; he first served Zhuangzong as a petty company commander and was promoted in succession to Shengjie army commander.

units.zh: 明宗登極，轉帳前都指揮使，領澶州刺史。
units.en: When Mingzong ascended the throne, Wu was made commander before the imperial tent and appointed prefect of Chanzhou.
units.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, Wu was transferred to commander before the imperial tent and held Chanzhou as prefect.

units.zh: 天成二年，改左羽林都指揮使，遙領宜州，充襄州都巡檢使。
units.en: In Tiancheng 2 he became commander of the Left Forest of Plumes army, held Yizhou in title only, and served as touring inspector of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was changed to Left Forest of Plumes army commander, held Yizhou in title only, and served as Xiangzhou touring inspector.

units.zh: 三年，自汴州馬步軍都指揮使授曹州刺史。
units.en: In the third year he was appointed prefect of Caozhou after serving as Bianzhou horse-and-foot army commander-in-chief.
units.literal: In the third year, from Bianzhou horse-and-foot army commander-in-chief he was appointed Caozhou prefect.

units.zh: 長興初，遷齊州防御史，又移洺州。
units.en: At the beginning of Changxing he was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou, then to Luozhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Changxing he was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou, then moved to Luozhou.

units.zh: 清泰中，歷成、隴二州，充西面行軍副部署。
units.en: During Qingtai he served in succession at Cheng and Long and was deputy deployment of the western campaign army.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he served in succession Cheng and Long prefectures and was deputy deployment of the western campaign army.

units.zh: 天福初，授金州防禦使，及金州建節鉞，武丁母憂，乃起復為節度使。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed defense commissioner of Jinzhou. When Jinzhou was elevated to a full military commission, Wu was mourning his mother but was recalled from mourning to serve as military commissioner.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed defense commissioner of Jinzhou; when Jinzhou received banners and axes Wu was in mourning for his mother but was recalled from mourning to serve as military commissioner.

units.zh: 開運元年，移鎮滄州，兼北面行營右廂都指揮使。
units.en: In Kaiyun 1 he was transferred to garrison Cangzhou and concurrently made Right Wing commander-in-chief of the Northern Campaign army.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun he was transferred to garrison Cangzhou and concurrently Right Wing commander-in-chief of the Northern Campaign army.

units.zh: 二年，授寧江軍節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the second year he was appointed military commissioner of the Ningjiang army and commander-in-chief of the palace guard infantry.
units.literal: In the second year he was appointed military commissioner of Ningjiang army and palace guard infantry commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 歲內改昭義軍節度、澤潞等州管內觀察處置等使、潞州大都督府長史、檢校太傅，封雁門郡開國公。
units.en: Within the year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, commissioner for observation and disposition of Ze, Lu, and other prefectures, senior administrator of the Lu metropolitan prefecture, acting Grand Tutor, and enfeoffed as Duke Who Opens the State of Yanmen commandery.
units.literal: Within the year he was changed to military commissioner of Zhaoyi army, commissioner charged with observation and disposition within Ze, Lu, and other prefectures, senior administrator of Lu Prefecture metropolitan commandery, acting Grand Tutor, and enfeoffed as Duke Who Opens the State of Yanmen commandery.

units.zh: 未赴任，以疾卒。
units.en: Before he could take up the post he died of illness.
units.literal: Before he could take up the post he died of illness.

units.zh: 武出身戎行，性鯁正，禦軍治民，鹹盡其善。
units.en: Wu came up through the ranks; he was upright by nature, and whether commanding troops or governing the people he did all to the best of his ability.
units.literal: Wu rose from the military profession; his nature was upright and firm. In commanding armies and governing the people he exhaustively applied his excellence.

units.zh: 及卒，朝廷惜之，詔贈太尉，輟視朝一日。
units.en: When he died the court mourned his loss, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal, and suspended court audiences for a day.
units.literal: When he died, the court regretted it and ordered him posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal, with court audiences suspended for one day.

units.zh: 子仁朗、仁遇並歷內職。
units.en: His sons Renlang and Renyu both served at court.
units.literal: His sons Renlang and Renyu both held inner-court posts.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史》：仁朗以父任西頭供奉官。）〉
units.en: (The History of Song records that Renlang received appointment as western-head attendant through his father's office.)〉
units.literal: (History of Song: Renlang entered office as western-head attendant through his father's position.)〉

units.zh: 李承福，字德華，漢陽人。
units.en: Li Chengfu, courtesy name Dehua, was a native of Hanyang.
units.literal: Li Chengfu, style name Dehua, was a man of Hanyang.

units.zh: 少寒賤，事元行欽掌皂棧之役，後為高祖家臣。
units.en: Born poor and lowly, he served Yuan Xingqin managing the stables and later became a household retainer of Gaozu.
units.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly, served Yuan Xingqin in charge of the stable duties, and later became a household retainer of Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖登極，歷皇城武德宣徽使、左千牛將軍，出為澶州刺史，遷齊州防禦使、檢校太保。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chengfu served as Wude palace treasury commissioner of the Imperial City and as Left Thousand-Ox general, was sent out as prefect of Chanzhou, and was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou and acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he served in succession as Wude palace treasury commissioner of the Imperial City and Left Thousand-Ox general, went out as Chanzhou prefect, and was transferred to Qizhou defense commissioner and acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 承福性鄙狹，無器局，好察人微事，多所詆訐，雖小過不能恕，工商之業，輿隸之情，官吏之幸，皆善知之，然自任所見，無所準的，故人多薄之。
units.en: Chengfu was mean-spirited and narrow-minded, without breadth of character. He pried into petty matters and slandered others relentlessly, forgiving not even small faults. He knew the trades of merchants and artisans, the gossip of servants, and the private fortunes of officials—but trusted only his own judgment, without consistent principle, and many despised him for it.
units.literal: Chengfu's nature was mean and narrow, without breadth of vision; he loved to scrutinize people's minute affairs and often slandered them, unable to forgive even small faults. The trades of artisans and merchants, the moods of carriage drivers and runners, and the fortunes of officials—he was skilled at knowing them all. Yet he trusted only his own views, with no fixed standard, and therefore many looked down on him.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，授同州節度使，尋卒於鎮。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was appointed military commissioner of Tongzhou and soon died in office.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was appointed Tongzhou military commissioner and soon died in his command.

units.zh: 少帝以高祖佐命之臣，聞之嗟嘆，賻物加等，輟視朝一日，詔贈太傅。
units.en: The Young Emperor, remembering him as one of Gaozu's founding ministers, sighed at the news, raised the funeral gifts by one grade, suspended court for a day, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Because he was a minister who had aided Gaozu in founding the dynasty, the Young Emperor sighed when he heard of it, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, suspended court audiences for one day, and ordered him posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 相裏金，字奉金，并州人也。
units.en: Xiangli Jin, courtesy name Fengjin, was a native of Bingzhou.
units.literal: Xiangli Jin, style name Fengjin, was a man of Bingzhou.

units.zh: 性勇悍果敢，能折節下士。
units.en: He was fierce, bold, and resolute, yet able to humble himself before men of talent.
units.literal: His nature was fierce, bold, and resolute, and he could humble himself to honor scholar-gentlemen.

units.zh: 唐景福初，武皇始置五院兵，金首預其選。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tang Jingfu era, when the Martial Emperor first established the Five-Court armies, Jin was among the first selected.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu era of Tang, the Martial Emperor first established the Five-Court armies, and Jin was among the first chosen.

units.zh: 從莊宗攻下夾寨，得補為小校，後與梁師戰於柏鄉及胡柳陂，以功授黃甲指揮使。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong in the capture of the stockaded camps and was made a junior officer. Later he fought Liang forces at Baixiang and Huliupo and, for his service, was appointed commander of the Yellow Armor corps.
units.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in capturing the stockaded camps and was appointed junior officer; later he fought Liang armies at Baixiang and Huliupo and, for merit, was made commander of the Yellow Armor corps.

units.zh: 同光中，統帳前軍拔中都，賜忠勇拱衛功臣、檢校刑部尚書。
units.en: During the Tongguang era he led the vanguard in the capture of Zhongdu and was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Valor and Imperial Guard and acting Minister of Justice.
units.literal: During Tongguang he commanded the vanguard army in capturing Zhongdu and was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Valor and Imperial Guard and acting Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 二年，自羽林都虞候出為忻州刺史，凡部曲私屬，皆不令干預民事，但優其贍給，使分掌家事而已，故郡民安之，大有聲績。
units.en: In the second year he left his post as Feathered Forest adjutant to become prefect of Xinzhou. He forbade his troops and personal retainers to meddle in civil affairs, contenting himself with generous support while they managed his household affairs alone. The prefecture lived in peace under him, and his reputation was excellent.
units.literal: In the second year he went out from Feathered Forest adjutant to Xinzhou prefect; all his troops and private dependents were forbidden to interfere in civil affairs—he only enriched their support and had them manage household affairs, and therefore the people of the prefecture were at peace and he won great reputation and achievement.

units.zh: 應順元年，為隴州防禦使，會唐末帝起兵於鳳翔，傳檄於鄰道，諸侯無應者，唯金遣判官薛文遇往來計事，末帝深德之。
units.en: In the first year of Yingshun he was defense commissioner of Longzhou. When the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops at Fengxiang and sent proclamations along the neighboring circuits, no other lord responded—only Jin sent his judicial officer Xue Wenyu to consult on strategy, for which the Last Emperor was deeply grateful.
units.literal: In the first year of Yingshun he was Longzhou defense commissioner. It happened that the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops at Fengxiang and sent proclamations to neighboring circuits; no regional lords responded except Jin, who sent his judicial officer Xue Wenyu back and forth to plan affairs—the Last Emperor was deeply grateful.

units.zh: 及即位，擢為陜州節度使加檢校太保。
units.en: When he took the throne, Jin was promoted to military commissioner of Shaanzhou and acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When he took the throne, Jin was promoted to Shaanzhou military commissioner with the added title acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 清泰三年夏，高祖建義於太原，唐末帝發兵來攻，以金為太原四面步軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the summer of the third year of Qingtai, when Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan and the Last Emperor of Tang sent troops against him, Jin was appointed overall commander of the foot forces encircling Taiyuan on all sides.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year of Qingtai, Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan; the Last Emperor of Tang sent troops to attack, and Jin was made overall commander of foot troops on all four sides of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 高祖即位，移鎮晉州，及受代歸闕，累為諸衛上將軍，加開府儀同三司，官至檢校太尉。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Jin was transferred to Jinzhou. After his term ended he returned to court and served repeatedly as supreme general of the guards, was given the rank of Palace Captain with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and rose to acting Grand Marshal.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Jin was transferred to garrison Jinzhou; when he was relieved and returned to court, he served repeatedly as supreme general of the guards, was given Palace Captain with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and reached the post of acting Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 爵列開國公，勛登上柱國，以久居散地，優之故也。
units.en: He held the noble rank of founding duke and the merit rank of Pillar of the State—honors granted because he had long served in lighter posts at court.
units.literal: His noble rank was Duke Who Founded the State; his merit rank was Pillar of the State—these honors were bestowed because he had long dwelt in posts without heavy duties.

units.zh: 天福五年夏，卒於任。
units.en: In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu he died in office.
units.literal: In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu, he died in office.

units.zh: 贈太師。
units.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 史臣曰：在禮之起甘陵也，當鼎革之期，會富貴來逼，既因人成事，亦何足自多。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Zaili's rise at Ganling came during a dynastic transition, when fortune pressed upon him. Having achieved his position through others' efforts, there was little cause for self-congratulation.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Zaili's rise at Ganling came at a time of dynastic transformation, when wealth and rank pressed upon him; since he accomplished the deed through others' efforts, what is there to boast of?

units.zh: 及其仗鉞擁旄，積財敗德，貨之為累，可不誡乎！
units.en: Once he bore commander's authority, he amassed wealth and ruined his virtue. How wealth can become a burden—surely this is a warning worth heeding!
units.literal: When he bore the battle-axe and grasped the banners, he amassed wealth and ruined his virtue—how wealth becomes a burden; is this not a lesson to heed!

units.zh: 全節之佐晉氏也，平安陸之妖，預宗城之戰，功既茂矣，貴亦宜然。
units.en: Quanjie's service to the Jin house included the pacification of Anlu and fighting at Zongcheng. His achievements were considerable, and his honors were deserved.
units.literal: Quanjie's assistance to the Jin house included pacifying the Anlu disturbance and taking part in the battle of Zongcheng; his merit was already abundant, and eminence was fitting.

units.zh: 張筠歷事累朝，享茲介福，蓋近代之幸人也。
units.en: Zhang Yun served successive dynasties and enjoyed such good fortune—among the men of recent times, he was singularly blessed.
units.literal: Zhang Yun served successive courts and enjoyed this measure of blessing—he was roughly a fortunate man of recent times.

units.zh: 自溫琪而下，皆服冕乘軒，苴茅燾土，垂名汗簡，詠亦宜焉。
units.en: From Wenqi onward, all wore court regalia and rode noble carriages, received feudal investiture, and left their names in the historical records—praise was fitting for them all.
units.literal: From Wenqi downward, all wore caps and rode carriages with high rails, received feudal investiture with thatch and earth, and left their names on the bamboo slips—praise was fitting for them as well.
